definition_en: completely, or only and nothing else
core_image: 一块布从头铺到尾，没有一寸遗漏
scene: 暴雨过后，整条山路都被泥水覆盖。After the storm, mud covered the mountain path entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 entirely 是「完全地」（第 1 个义项：在程度或范围上毫无遗漏）；句意：暴雨过后，泥水把山路完全盖住了。

senses.title: Completely, in every part
senses.definition: in every part or to the full degree, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 在每一部分上或达到十足程度，没有任何遗漏
senses.example: I agree with you entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to entire, so it describes something done in a whole and complete way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 entire 加 -ly 构成，所以描述以完整、彻底的方式完成某事。

senses.title: Solely, and nothing else
senses.definition: used to say that something is only or wholly due to one thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事仅仅或完全由于某一原因
senses.example: The decision was entirely hers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定完全是她做的。
senses.why: If something is whole, nothing else is mixed in, so entirely can mean solely.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物是完整的，就没有别的东西掺入，因此 entirely 可以表示「仅仅」。

senses.title: Fully and without reservation
senses.definition: with complete commitment or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 带着完全的投入或赞同
senses.example: She trusted him entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全信任他。
senses.why: Complete agreement leaves no room for doubt, which gives the sense of full-hearted trust.
senses.whyCN: 完全的赞同不留怀疑余地，于是产生「全心信任」的含义。

intro.en: Entirely is the adverb of entire, which comes from Latin integer, whole and untouched, through Old French entier.
intro.cn: entirely 是 entire 的副词形式；entire 来自拉丁语 integer（完整、未被触碰），经古法语 entier 进入英语。

items.en: Tangere means to touch or handle.
items.cn: tangere 意为触碰或接触。

items.en: In- here means not.
items.cn: 这里的 in- 表示「不」。

items.en: Integer means whole and untouched.
items.cn: integer 意为完整的、未被触碰的。

items.en: Entier keeps the sense of whole and complete.
items.cn: entier 保留「完整、完全」的意思。

items.en: Entire describes something whole and sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 entire 描述完整而完好之物。

items.en: The adverb entirely means completely or solely.
items.cn: 现代英语副词 entirely 表示完全地或仅仅。

note.en: Entirely belongs to the entire family and sits close to adverbs for complete degree.
note.cn: entirely 属于 entire 词族，并与表示完全程度的副词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Entirely is simply entire plus -ly: whatever is whole is done in a whole way.
normalIntro.cn: entirely 就是 entire 加 -ly：完整的东西，就以完整的方式去做。

normal.en: Entire means whole, so entirely means in a whole way.
normal.cn: entire 意为完整，所以 entirely 表示以完整的方式。

normal.en: Not entirely sure means not completely sure.
normal.cn: not entirely sure 就是不完全确定。

normal.en: The phrase entirely up to you means completely your choice.
normal.cn: 短语 entirely up to you 表示完全由你决定。

normal.en: Entirely can also mean solely, as in entirely her fault.
normal.cn: entirely 也可表示「仅仅」，如 entirely her fault。

normal.en: Compare partly, its opposite in degree.
normal.cn: 对比 partly，它是程度上的反义词。

abstract.en: Picture a blank sheet with no edge torn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张空白纸，边缘一处也没有撕破。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp lighting every corner of one room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮一个房间的每个角落。

abstract.en: Think of a full glass filled to the very brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃杯被倒到最满。

examples.en: The room was entirely empty when we arrived.
examples.cn: 我们到达时，房间完全是空的。

examples.en: Her answer was not entirely honest.
examples.cn: 她的回答并不完全诚实。

examples.en: The program is entirely free for students.
examples.cn: 这个项目对学生完全免费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tire」——轮胎一个都没落下，整辆车都齐全；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）＋ tangere（触碰）→ integer（完整无缺）→ 古法语 entier → entire ＋ -ly → entirely，核心义「完整地、完全地」。

sensesIntro.en: Entirely first means in every part, then narrows to solely, and finally describes full-hearted commitment.
sensesIntro.cn: entirely 先表示在每一部分上，再收窄为「仅仅」，最后描述毫无保留的投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sheet spread out with no corner missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块布铺开，没有缺角。

branches.en: Completeness in every part is the main adverbial sense.
branches.cn: 每一部分都完整，是主要副词义项。

branches.en: Wholeness with nothing mixed in gives the sense of solely.
branches.cn: 完整而没有别物掺入，产生「仅仅」的含义。

branches.en: Complete agreement extends the idea to full trust.
branches.cn: 完全的赞同把这一概念扩展到全心信任。

branches.en: Doing something completely often means doing it wholeheartedly.
branches.cn: 完全地做某事，往往意味着全身心投入。

branches.en: A decision made solely by one person can be trusted entirely.
branches.cn: 完全由一个人做出的决定，也可以被完全信任。

intro.en: Entirely is a Latin adjective reshaped by French, with the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: entirely 是经法语改造的拉丁形容词，加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer means whole or untouched, from in-, not, and tangere, to touch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer 意为完整或未被触碰，由 in-（不）与 tangere（触碰）构成。

items.exampleCN: in- 在 integer 中否定 tangere。

items.example: Tangere supplies the idea of touch.
Integer is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: integer 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Entier carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entier 把这个词带入法语。
entirely 表示在每一部分上。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
表示状态或性质的词尾

items.example: Entireness is a rare synonym of entirety.
items.exampleCN: entireness 是 entirety 的罕见同义词。

definition_zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名
definition_en: to give someone a right, or to give a title to something
core_image: 一张写着名字的证件，让人有资格走进门内
scene: 公司规定，工作满一年的员工可以享受额外假期。The company entitles every worker with a year of service to extra holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 entitles 是 entitle 的第三人称单数，表示「使有权享受」（第 1 个义项：赋予某人权利或资格）；句意：公司让工作满一年的员工有权享受额外假期。

pos.zh: 使有权；给予资格；给……命名

senses.title: To give someone a right
senses.definition: to give a person the legal or moral right to have or do something
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某人拥有或做某事的法律或道义权利
senses.example: The law entitles citizens to free medical care.
senses.exampleCN: 法律使公民有权享受免费医疗。
senses.why: En- adds a sense of putting someone into a state, and title supplies the legal claim, so the verb means to grant a right.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 表示使人进入某种状态，title 提供法律主张的含义，所以这个动词表示授予权利。

senses.title: To give a title to a work
senses.definition: to give a name or title to a book, film, song, or other work
senses.definitionCN: 给书、电影、歌曲或其他作品起名称
senses.example: The author entitled her first novel The Long Road.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把她的第一部小说命名为《长路》。
senses.why: Title also means the name of a work, so to entitle is to put a title on it.
senses.whyCN: title 也指作品的名称，因此 entitle 就是给作品加上标题。

senses.title: To give a name or label to a person
senses.definition: to give someone a particular name, label, or description
senses.definitionCN: 给某人一个特定的称呼、标签或描述
senses.example: Critics entitled him the voice of his generation.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称他为那一代人的声音。
senses.why: A title can be an honor or a label, so the verb extends from naming works to naming people.
senses.whyCN: 称号既可以是荣誉也可以是标签，所以这个动词从给作品命名扩展到称呼人。

intro.en: Entitle comes from Latin titulus, a title or label, through Old French entitler, meaning to give a title to.
intro.cn: entitle 来自拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号），经古法语 entitler（给……加标题）进入英语。

items.en: Titulus means a title, label, or inscription.
items.cn: titulus 意为标题、标签或铭文。

items.en: Intitulare means to give a title to something.
items.cn: intitulare 意为给某物加上标题。

items.en: Entitler carries the legal and naming senses.
items.cn: entitler 同时带有法律与命名的含义。

items.en: Entitle means both to name and to give a claim.
items.cn: 中古英语 entitle 既表示命名，也表示赋予权利。

items.en: Modern English keeps the right sense in be entitled to.
items.cn: 现代英语在 be entitled to 中保留「有权」的含义。

note.en: Entitle is a giving word: it gives rights or names, so its company includes title words and words for granting.
note.cn: entitle 是一个「给予」词：给予权利或名称，所以它与 title 词族及表示授予的词相邻。

entries.definition: the name of a work or a rank
having a right or a title
to give official power or permission
to give a name to something

normalIntro.en: Entitle is en- plus title: to put someone or something into a title, whether a legal claim or a name.
normalIntro.cn: entitle 是 en- 加 title：把人或事物放进一个「名分」里，既可以是法律权利，也可以是名称。

normal.en: A ticket entitles you to a seat, and the verb entitles you to a right.
normal.cn: 一张票让你有座位，动词 entitle 让你有权利。

normal.en: Be entitled to means have the right to.
normal.cn: be entitled to 表示有权享有。

normal.en: A book is entitled, and so is a film.
normal.cn: 书可以被命名，电影也可以。

normal.en: The noun entitlement names the right itself.
normal.cn: 名词 entitlement 指权利本身。

normal.en: Compare title: title is the name, entitle is the act of giving it.
normal.cn: 对比 title：title 是名称，entitle 是给予名称的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a key being placed into a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被放进一双等待的手中。

abstract.en: Imagine a label being tied to a new book.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标签被系在一本新书上。

abstract.en: Think of a name written at the top of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写在页面顶端。

examples.en: This pass entitles you to enter the gallery.
examples.cn: 这张通行证使你有权进入画廊。

examples.en: She entitled her essay A Quiet Morning.
examples.cn: 她把自己的文章命名为《安静的早晨》。

examples.en: The ticket entitles each visitor to one free drink.
examples.cn: 这张票让每位参观者有权获得一杯免费饮料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + title」——给你一个「头衔」，你就有资格；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 titulus（标题、称号）→ 拉丁语 intitulare（加标题）→ 古法语 entitler → 中古英语 entitle，核心义「给予名分」，引申为赋予权利。

sensesIntro.en: Entitle moves from granting a legal claim to giving a work a title, and then to giving a person a label.
sensesIntro.cn: entitle 从授予法律权利，扩展到给作品加标题，再扩展到给人加称号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document with a name on it that opens a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写有名字、可以打开一扇门的文书。

branches.en: Granting a right is the dominant legal sense.
branches.cn: 授予权利，是主要的法律义项。

branches.en: Giving a work its name keeps the original title idea.
branches.cn: 给作品命名，保留最初的「标题」概念。

branches.en: Giving a person a label extends naming to people.
branches.cn: 给人加称号，把命名扩展到人。

branches.en: Both rights and titles are things formally granted.
branches.cn: 权利与称号都是被正式授予的东西。

branches.en: A person can be legally entitled and publicly entitled.
branches.cn: 一个人可以依法有权，也可以被公开称呼。

intro.en: Entitle is built from en-, a Latin title word, and English endings for the derived forms.
intro.cn: entitle 由 en-、拉丁语 title 词根以及构成派生形式的英语词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin titulus means a title or inscription, and intitulare means to give a title.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 titulus 意为标题或铭文，intitulare 意为加上标题。

items.example: En- puts a person into a titled state.
items.exampleCN: en- 把人带入拥有名分的状态。

items.example: Titulus is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: titulus 是这个词族的词根。

items.example: Intitulare adds the Latin verb form.
items.exampleCN: intitulare 提供拉丁语动词形式。

items.example: Entitler brings the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entitler 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: to give a right or title
items.exampleCN: entitle 同时保留两种含义。

items.meaning: forming a past form or adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成过去式或形容词的词尾

items.example: Entitled describes someone with a claim.
items.exampleCN: entitled 描述拥有权利的人。

items.example: Title is the shorter noun beside the verb.
items.exampleCN: title 是与动词并存的较短名词。

definition_zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入
definition_en: a way in, an item in a list, or a thing entered in a competition
core_image: 一扇门通向里面的房间，门边还挂着一块记录牌
scene: 博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。The side entry of the museum is open only to staff.
sceneCN: 这里 entry 是「入口」（第 1 个义项：进入的通道或门）；句意：博物馆的侧门只对工作人员开放。

pos.zh: 入口；条目；参赛作品；进入

senses.title: A way in
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage through which one enters
senses.definitionCN: 供人进入的门、大门或通道
senses.example: The side entry was blocked by boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 侧面的入口被箱子堵住了。
senses.why: Entry first names the act of going in, and then the place where that act happens.
senses.whyCN: entry 最初指进入的动作，随后指发生这一动作的地方。

senses.title: An item in a list or record
senses.definition: a single item written in a list, diary, dictionary, or record
senses.definitionCN: 写在清单、日记、词典或记录中的单项
senses.example: He wrote a short entry in his diary.
senses.exampleCN: 他在日记里写了一条简短的记录。
senses.why: What is entered into a book becomes an entry, so the word names one recorded item.
senses.whyCN: 被写进书里的内容成为 entry，因此这个词指一条被记录的项目。

senses.title: A competition submission
senses.definition: a person or work entered in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 报名参加比赛的人或作品
senses.example: Her entry won the photography prize.
senses.exampleCN: 她的参赛作品赢得了摄影奖。
senses.why: To enter a contest is to put something in, and the thing put in is the entry.
senses.whyCN: 参加比赛就是把某物投进去，被投进去的东西就是 entry。

senses.title: The act of entering
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, group, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 进入某地、加入某团体或协定的行为
senses.example: The country's entry into the trade agreement took years.
senses.exampleCN: 该国加入这项贸易协定花了好几年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply the act of going in, which still appears in formal phrases.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义就是进入的动作，这一含义仍出现在正式短语中。

intro.en: Entry comes from Latin intrare, to enter, through Old French entree, and it keeps both the act and the place of entering.
intro.cn: entry 来自拉丁语 intrare（进入），经古法语 entree 进入英语，同时保留「进入的动作」与「进入之处」两层含义。

items.en: Intrare means to go in or enter.
items.cn: intrare 意为走进去、进入。

items.en: Intro means within or inside.
items.cn: intro 意为在内部。

items.en: Entree names both the act and the place of entering.
items.cn: entree 同时指进入的动作和进入的地点。

items.en: Entry appears with the same double sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 entry 出现时也带有这双重含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a recorded item.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「记录条目」的含义。

note.en: Entry is a going-in word and a record word, so it sits near enter words and near words for access.
note.cn: entry 既表示「进入」，也表示「记录」，因此与 enter 词族及表示通行的词相邻。

entries.definition: a way in or the act of entering
a door or passage for entering
the right or way to enter

normalIntro.en: Entry is the noun of enter: the way in, the act of going in, or the thing you put into a list.
normalIntro.cn: entry 是 enter 的名词：进去的路、进去的动作，或你写进清单里的那一项。

normal.en: No entry means you may not go in.
normal.cn: no entry 表示禁止进入。

normal.en: A dictionary entry is one word and its explanation.
normal.cn: dictionary entry 是一个词及其解释。

normal.en: An entry form is the paper you fill in to join.
normal.cn: entry form 是报名时填写的表格。

normal.en: The plural entries covers lists and contestants alike.
normal.cn: 复数 entries 既可指多条记录，也可指多位参赛者。

normal.en: Compare entrance: entrance stresses the doorway, entry suits records and contests too.
normal.cn: 对比 entrance：entrance 强调门口，entry 还适用于记录和比赛。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow gate with a small sign beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇窄门，旁边挂着一块小牌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a line written neatly in a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象笔记本上工整地写着一行字。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed box waiting on a contest table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个封好的盒子放在比赛桌上等待评审。

examples.en: The back entry leads to a small garden.
examples.cn: 后门通向一个小花园。

examples.en: Each entry in the list has a date.
examples.cn: 清单上的每一条记录都有一个日期。

examples.en: The judges praised the youngest entry.
examples.cn: 评委称赞了最年轻的参赛作品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + try」——想进去就得试一试；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entree（进入；入口）→ 中古英语 entry，核心义「进入」，引申为入口与记录条目。

sensesIntro.en: Entry begins with the act of going in, then names the place, the recorded item, and the thing submitted to a contest.
sensesIntro.cn: entry 从进入的动作开始，随后指进入之处、被记录的项目以及提交参赛的作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway, with a ledger open nearby.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，旁边摊开一本登记簿。

branches.en: The doorway is the place of entering.
branches.cn: 入口是进入发生的地点。

branches.en: A recorded item is what has been entered in a book.
branches.cn: 记录条目是被写进书里的内容。

branches.en: A contest entry is what has been entered in a competition.
branches.cn: 参赛作品是被投进比赛的东西。

branches.en: The bare act of entering is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 纯粹的进入动作是最古老的含义。

branches.en: A doorway exists for the act of entering.
branches.cn: 入口正是为了进入的动作而存在。

intro.en: Entry grows from Latin intrare and Old French entree, with English relatives enter, entrance, and entrant.
intro.cn: entry 源自拉丁语 intrare 与古法语 entree，英语亲属词有 enter、entrance 与 entrant。

latinIntro.en: Latin intrare means to enter, built on intra, within.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为进入，建立在 intra（在内）之上。

items.example: Intra marks the inside of a place.
items.exampleCN: intra 标示一个地方的内部。

items.example: Intrare is the direct Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: intrare 是直接的拉丁语动词。

items.example: Entree carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: entree 把这个词带入法语。

items.meaning: a way in or a recorded item
items.exampleCN: entry 保留两种古老含义。

items.example: Enter is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: enter 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: An entrant is someone who enters.
The ending of entry marks a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: entry 的词尾标示动作名词。

definition_en: a paper cover for a letter, or any enclosing cover
core_image: 一张纸把信折包在里面，只露出封口
scene: 她把照片放进棕色信封，写上地址。She put the photo in a brown envelope and wrote the address.
sceneCN: 这里 envelope 是「信封」（第 1 个义项：装信件或文件的纸套）；句意：她把照片装进棕色信封并写上地址。

senses.title: A paper cover for a letter
senses.definition: a flat paper container used for sending letters or papers
senses.definitionCN: 用于寄送信件或文件的扁平纸制容器
senses.example: He sealed the envelope and mailed it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信封封好并寄了出去。
senses.why: The word comes from a French verb meaning to wrap, so the paper wrapper for a letter is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「包裹」的法语动词，所以装信件的纸套是它的第一个义项。

senses.title: Any enclosing cover
senses.definition: a layer or cover that wraps something around
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从四周包起来的层或罩
senses.example: A thin envelope of dust covered the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子上覆着一层薄薄的灰尘。
senses.why: The idea of wrapping extends from paper to any surrounding layer.
senses.whyCN: 「包裹」的概念从纸张扩展到任何包围的层。

senses.title: The limit of what is accepted
senses.definition: the boundary of what is normal or possible, especially in performance
senses.definitionCN: 正常或可能范围的边界，尤指表现方面
senses.example: The test pilots pushed the envelope of speed.
senses.exampleCN: 试飞员挑战了速度的极限。
senses.why: Aircraft have a safe operating envelope, and pushing beyond it became a general image for testing limits.
senses.whyCN: 飞机有安全运行包线，越过它就成了一般意义上「挑战极限」的意象。

senses.title: A technical outer membrane
senses.definition: a membrane or outer layer enclosing a cell, virus, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 包住细胞、病毒或结构的膜或外层
senses.example: The virus is wrapped in a protein envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒外面包着一层蛋白质外膜。
senses.why: The biological sense applies the same enclosing idea at a microscopic scale.
senses.whyCN: 生物学义项把同样的包裹概念用于微观尺度。

intro.en: Envelope comes from Old French envoloper, to wrap, which goes back to Latin volvere, to roll or turn.
intro.cn: envelope 来自古法语 envoloper（包裹），其根源是拉丁语 volvere（卷、转）。

items.en: Volvere means to roll or turn around.
items.cn: volvere 意为卷动或转动。

items.en: Voloper develops the sense of wrapping.
items.cn: voloper 发展出「包裹」的含义。

items.en: Envoloper means to wrap something up.
items.cn: envoloper 意为把某物包起来。

items.en: Enveloppe names the wrapper itself.
items.cn: enveloppe 指包裹物本身。

items.en: English envelope first means a wrapper and then a letter cover.
items.cn: 英语 envelope 先指包裹物，再指信封。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical senses of limit and membrane.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「极限」与「外膜」等技术义项。

note.en: Envelope is a wrapping noun, closely tied to the verb envelop and to words for covers.
note.cn: envelope 是表示包裹的名词，与动词 envelop 以及表示覆盖的词关系紧密。

entries.definition: the act of wrapping or surrounding

normalIntro.en: Envelope is the noun of envelop: it is the thing that wraps a letter and holds it inside.
normalIntro.cn: envelope 是 envelop 的名词：它就是包住信件、把信装在里面的事物。

normal.en: A sealed envelope hides the letter until it is opened.
normal.cn: 封好的信封把信藏起来，直到被打开。

normal.en: To push the envelope is to test a limit.
normal.cn: push the envelope 就是挑战极限。

normal.en: The verb envelop means to wrap, with no final e sound.
normal.cn: 动词 envelop 意为包裹，结尾不读长音。

normal.en: A biological envelope is an outer membrane.
normal.cn: 生物学中的 envelope 是外膜。

normal.en: Compare wrapper: wrapper is general, envelope is usually paper for mail.
normal.cn: 对比 wrapper：wrapper 更泛指包装，envelope 通常指邮寄用的纸套。

abstract.en: Picture two paper flaps folding over a sealed letter.
abstract.cn: 想象两片纸翼折过来盖住一封封好的信。

abstract.en: Imagine a thin ring of dust around a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯周围有一圈薄薄的灰尘。

abstract.en: Think of a plane flying at the edge of its safe range.
abstract.cn: 想象一架飞机飞在安全范围的边缘。

examples.en: She licked the envelope and pressed it shut.
examples.cn: 她舔了舔信封，把它压紧封好。

examples.en: A soft envelope of mist lay over the field.
examples.cn: 田野上覆着一层柔和的薄雾。

examples.en: Engineers keep testing the envelope of the new design.
examples.cn: 工程师们不断测试新设计的性能极限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + velope」——把信「包」进纸里，就成信封；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（卷、转）→ 古法语 envoloper（包裹）→ enveloppe（包裹物）→ 英语 envelope，核心义「包在外面的套子」。

sensesIntro.en: Envelope starts as a paper wrapper, extends to any enclosing layer, then to a boundary of performance and a biological membrane.
sensesIntro.cn: envelope 从纸信封开始，扩展到任何包围层，再扩展到性能界限与生物外膜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paper folded around a letter, sealed on all sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸从四面折起包住一封信并封好。

branches.en: The mail cover is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 邮寄用的纸套是日常义项。

branches.en: Any enclosing layer extends the wrap idea.
branches.cn: 任何包围层都扩展了「包裹」的概念。

branches.en: The safe operating range became an image for limits.
branches.cn: 安全运行包线成为「极限」的意象。

branches.en: The biological membrane applies the outer-layer sense.
branches.cn: 生物外膜运用了「外层」义项。

branches.en: Both a letter cover and a dust layer enclose something.
branches.cn: 信封与灰尘层都把某物包在里面。

intro.en: Envelope belongs to the volvere family of wrapping words, with the verb envelop and the noun envelopment.
intro.cn: envelope 属于 volvere 这一「包裹」词族，另有动词 envelop 与名词 envelopment。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere means to roll, and involvere means to wrap around.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为卷动，involvere 意为缠绕包裹。

items.example: Involvere adds the sense of enclosing.
Envoloper is the French wrapping verb.
items.exampleCN: envoloper 是法语中表示包裹的动词。

definition_zh: 环境；周围状况；自然环境
definition_en: the natural world, or the conditions around a person or thing
core_image: 一圈空气、景物与人声把一个人围在中间
scene: 孩子们在安静的环境里读书。The children read in a quiet environment.
sceneCN: 这里 environment 是「周围状况」（第 2 个义项：影响人或事物的周边条件）；句意：孩子们在安静的环境中读书。

pos.zh: 环境；周围状况；自然环境

senses.title: The natural world
senses.definition: the air, water, land, and living things around us, especially when seen as needing protection
senses.definitionCN: 我们周围的空气、水、土地与生物，尤指需要保护的整体
senses.example: We must protect the environment for future generations.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须为子孙后代保护环境。
senses.why: The word names what surrounds us, and in modern use the whole natural world is the most prominent surround.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指围绕我们的一切，而在现代用法中，整个自然界是最突出的「周围」。

senses.title: Surrounding conditions
senses.definition: the conditions, people, and influences around a person or activity
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某人或某项活动的条件、人与影响
senses.example: A calm environment helps children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 平静的环境有助于孩子学习。
senses.why: The core sense is simply what surrounds, so it applies to homes, schools, and workplaces.
senses.whyCN: 核心含义就是「围绕之物」，因此适用于家庭、学校和工作场所。

senses.title: A computing runtime setting
senses.definition: the software and hardware setting in which a program runs
senses.definitionCN: 程序运行所依赖的软件与硬件设置
senses.example: The program runs in a virtual environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序在虚拟环境中运行。
senses.why: Technical usage treats the surrounding system as the environment of a program.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法把围绕程序的系统视为它的环境。

intro.en: Environment comes from Old French environ, around, plus the noun suffix -ment, so it literally means the state of being surrounded.
intro.cn: environment 来自古法语 environ（在周围）加名词词尾 -ment，字面意思是「被围绕的状态」。

items.en: Viron means a circle or a turn.
items.cn: viron 意为圆圈或一圈。

items.en: Environ means around or surrounding.
items.cn: environ 意为在周围、围绕。

items.en: Environnement names the surrounding conditions.
items.cn: environnement 指周围的条件。

items.en: English environment first means surroundings in general.
items.cn: 英语 environment 最初泛指周围事物。

items.en: Modern English adds the natural world and computing senses.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「自然界」与计算机义项。

note.en: Environment is a surrounding word, with a large family of adjectives and a set of near synonyms for settings.
note.cn: environment 是表示「周围」的词，拥有庞大的形容词词族，以及一组表示场景的近义词。

entries.definition: a person who works to protect nature
everything around a place or person
the place and conditions of an event
the natural home of a plant or animal

normalIntro.en: Environment is environ plus -ment: the condition of being circled by things.
normalIntro.cn: environment 是 environ 加 -ment：被事物围在中间的状态。

normal.en: Environ means around, so environment is what is around you.
normal.cn: environ 意为在周围，所以 environment 就是你周围的一切。

normal.en: The natural environment is the whole living world.
normal.cn: natural environment 指整个生命世界。

normal.en: The adjective environmental appears in environmental protection.
normal.cn: 形容词 environmental 出现在「环境保护」中。

normal.en: An environmentalist works to protect nature.
normal.cn: environmentalist 是致力于保护自然的人。

normal.en: Compare surroundings: surroundings is more local and physical.
normal.cn: 对比 surroundings：surroundings 更偏局部和物理层面。

abstract.en: Picture a soft ring of air drawn around a standing figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一个站立的人周围画着一圈柔和的气。

abstract.en: Imagine a forest folded around a small village.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林把一个小村庄环抱起来。

abstract.en: Think of a program sitting inside a glowing frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一个程序坐在发光的框架之内。

examples.en: The factory promised to protect the local environment.
examples.cn: 这家工厂承诺保护当地环境。

examples.en: A friendly environment makes new students feel welcome.
examples.cn: 友好的环境让新生感到受欢迎。

examples.en: Developers tested the app in a secure environment.
examples.cn: 开发者在安全的环境中测试了这个应用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + viron」——把你「围」在中间的一切，就是环境；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 environ（在周围）＋ -ment → environment，核心义「被围绕的状态」，引申为周围条件与自然环境。

sensesIntro.en: Environment starts as whatever surrounds us, then narrows to the natural world, and later extends to the setting of a program.
sensesIntro.cn: environment 从「围绕我们的一切」开始，收窄为自然界，后来又扩展到程序的运行环境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of air and scenery drawn around a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人周围画着一圈空气与景物。

branches.en: The natural world is the dominant public sense.
branches.cn: 自然界是主要的公共义项。

branches.en: Surrounding conditions keep the oldest spatial sense.
branches.cn: 周围条件保留最古老的空间含义。

branches.en: A runtime setting extends surroundings to software.
branches.cn: 运行环境把「周围」扩展到软件。

branches.en: The natural world is also the largest set of conditions around us.
branches.cn: 自然界也是围绕我们最大的条件集合。

branches.en: Both a classroom and a server provide conditions for activity.
branches.cn: 教室与服务器都为活动提供条件。

intro.en: Environment is environ plus -ment, and its family grows with -al, -ly, and -ist.
intro.cn: environment 由 environ 加 -ment 构成，词族再由 -al、-ly 与 -ist 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The French verb environ, to surround, goes back to viron, a circle or turn.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词 environ（围绕）可追溯到 viron（圆圈、一圈）。

items.example: Viron gives the image of a circle.

items.exampleCN: environment 指围绕我们的事物。

items.example: Environmentally means with regard to nature.

definition_zh: 环境的；有关环境的；环保的
definition_en: relating to the natural world or to the conditions around something
core_image: 一圈森林和水流围住城市，边上竖着检测牌
scene: 这家公司因违反环保法规而被罚款。The company was fined for breaking environmental rules.
sceneCN: 这里 environmental 是「有关环境的」（第 1 个义项：与自然环境相关）；句意：这家公司因违反环保法规而被罚款。

pos.zh: 环境的；有关环境的；环保的

senses.title: Relating to the natural world
senses.definition: connected with the air, water, land, and living things that surround us
senses.definitionCN: 与我们周围的空气、水、土地和生物相关的
senses.example: The report lists the main environmental problems of the region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了该地区的主要环境问题。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds -al to environment, and the dominant noun sense is the natural world.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是 environment 加 -al，而该名词的主要义项是自然界。

senses.title: Relating to surrounding conditions
senses.definition: connected with the conditions that surround a person, place, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 与围绕某人、某地或某项活动的条件有关的
senses.example: Noise is a serious environmental factor in city schools.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音是城市学校中一个严重的环境因素。
senses.why: The older sense of surroundings still appears when conditions rather than nature are meant.
senses.whyCN: 当所指为条件而非自然时，仍会出现「周围环境」这一较老的含义。

senses.title: Designed to protect nature
senses.definition: designed or intended to reduce harm to the natural world
senses.definitionCN: 旨在减少对自然界的损害的
senses.example: They chose an environmental heating system for the new house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为新房选择了一套环保供暖系统。
senses.why: Because the natural world needs protection, the adjective often carries the practical sense of being eco-friendly.
senses.whyCN: 由于自然界需要保护，这个形容词常带有「对环保有利」的实用含义。

intro.en: Environmental is environment plus -al, tracing back through French environ, around, to viron, a circle.
intro.cn: environmental 是 environment 加 -al，可经法语 environ（在周围）追溯到 viron（圆圈）。

items.en: Viron means a circle or a turn.
items.cn: viron 意为圆圈或一圈。

items.en: Environ means around.
items.cn: environ 意为在周围。

items.en: Environnement names the surroundings.
items.cn: environnement 指周围环境。

items.en: Environment becomes the noun for surroundings.
items.cn: 英语 environment 成为表示周围环境的名词。

items.en: The adjective environmental adds -al and spreads into policy and science.
items.cn: 形容词 environmental 加 -al，并扩展到政策与科学领域。

note.en: Environmental is the adjective of environment, and it sits near other words for ecological concern.
note.cn: environmental 是 environment 的形容词，并与表示生态关切的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to living things and their homes

normalIntro.en: Environmental is environment with -al, so it describes anything belonging to the surroundings.
normalIntro.cn: environmental 是 environment 加 -al，因此描述任何属于周围环境的事物。

normal.en: Environmental protection means keeping nature safe.
normal.cn: environmental protection 指保护自然。

normal.en: Environmental law controls pollution.
normal.cn: environmental law 管控污染。

normal.en: An environmental impact is an effect on nature.
normal.cn: environmental impact 是对自然的影响。

normal.en: The adverb environmentally appears in environmentally friendly.
normal.cn: 副词 environmentally 出现在 environmentally friendly 中。

normal.en: Compare ecological: ecological is more scientific, environmental is broader.
normal.cn: 对比 ecological：ecological 更偏科学，environmental 范围更广。

abstract.en: Picture a green ring drawn around a crowded city.
abstract.cn: 想象一座拥挤的城市外围画着一圈绿色。

abstract.en: Imagine a label on a product that shows a small leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象产品标签上画着一片小叶子。

abstract.en: Think of a scientist measuring the air above a factory.
abstract.cn: 想象科学家在测量工厂上方的空气。

examples.en: Environmental damage can take decades to repair.
examples.cn: 环境破坏可能需要几十年才能修复。

examples.en: The school joined a national environmental campaign.
examples.cn: 这所学校参加了全国性的环保活动。

examples.en: They bought environmental cleaning products for the office.
examples.cn: 他们为办公室购买了环保清洁用品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「environment + al」——给「环境」加上形容词尾巴，就变成「环境的」；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 environ（在周围）＋ -ment ＋ -al → environmental，核心义「与周围环境有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Environmental begins with the natural world, still covers surrounding conditions, and often means actively friendly to nature.
sensesIntro.cn: environmental 从自然界开始，仍涵盖周围条件，并常表示积极有利于自然。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of nature drawn around human activity.
core.cn: 核心意象：人类活动周围画着一圈自然。

branches.en: The natural-world sense is the main modern use.
branches.cn: 自然界的义项是现代主要用法。

branches.en: Surrounding conditions keep the older spatial sense.
branches.cn: 周围条件保留较老的空间含义。

branches.en: Being friendly to nature is a practical extension.
branches.cn: 对自然友好是实用的延伸。

branches.en: Nature is the largest set of conditions around us.
branches.cn: 自然界是围绕我们最大的条件集合。

branches.en: Protecting nature is the aim behind green choices.
branches.cn: 保护自然是环保选择背后的目标。

intro.en: Environmental stacks -al on environment, itself environ plus -ment.
intro.cn: environmental 在 environment 上叠加 -al，而 environment 本身是 environ 加 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The French verb environ, to surround, comes from viron, a circle.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词 environ（围绕）来自 viron（圆圈）。

items.example: Environmentally stresses the point of view.
items.exampleCN: environmentally 强调看问题的角度。

definition_en: the feeling of wanting what someone else has, or to feel that way
core_image: 一个人盯着别人手里的果子，自己的手却空着
scene: 看到朋友的奖杯时，他心里生出一丝嫉妒。A touch of envy rose in him when he saw his friend's trophy.
sceneCN: 这里 envy 是「嫉妒」（第 1 个义项：因别人拥有而心生不快或渴望）；句意：看到朋友的奖杯，他心里生出一丝嫉妒。

senses.title: The feeling of wanting another's good
senses.definition: an unhappy or longing feeling caused by someone else's possessions, qualities, or luck
senses.definitionCN: 因他人的财物、品质或运气而产生的不快或渴望
senses.example: Her success filled him with envy.
senses.exampleCN: 她的成功让他满心嫉妒。
senses.why: The Latin root means to look at someone with a grudging eye, which is exactly the feeling of envy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为带着不满的眼光看人，这正是嫉妒的感受。

senses.title: The person or thing envied
senses.definition: a person or thing that others wish they had
senses.definitionCN: 别人希望自己也能拥有的人或物
senses.example: Their garden is the envy of the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的花园让整条街的人羡慕。
senses.why: The feeling and its object share one word, so envy can name the admired thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 感受与对象共用一词，所以 envy 也可以指被羡慕的事物本身。

senses.title: To feel envy toward someone
senses.definition: to feel unhappy longing because another person has something
senses.definitionCN: 因别人拥有某物而感到不快而渴望
senses.example: He envied his brother's easy confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他嫉妒哥哥那份从容的自信。
senses.why: The verb turns the feeling into an action directed at a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词形式把这股感受变成指向某人的动作。

intro.en: Envy comes from Latin invidia, from invidere, to look upon with malice, built on in-, against, and videre, to see.
intro.cn: envy 来自拉丁语 invidia，源自动词 invidere（带着恶意看），由 in-（对着）与 videre（看）构成。

items.en: Videre means to see.
items.cn: videre 意为看见。

items.en: Invidere means to look at with a hostile eye.
items.cn: invidere 意为带着敌意看。

items.en: Invidia names the feeling of envy.
items.cn: invidia 指嫉妒这种感受。

items.en: Envie carries the word into French.
items.cn: envie 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Envy appears in English with the same hostile longing.
items.cn: 中古英语 envy 带着同样的敌意渴望出现。

items.en: Modern English also uses envy for a milder wish to have something.
items.cn: 现代英语也用 envy 表示较温和的「希望拥有」。

note.en: Envy is a seeing-rooted feeling word, close to its envious family and to jealousy.
note.cn: envy 是一个源于「看」的感受词，与 envious 词族以及 jealousy 相邻。

entries.definition: likely to cause envy or offense
fear of losing what one has to a rival
to want something belonging to another
to feel unhappy about another's good fortune

normalIntro.en: Envy comes from looking: the envious eye keeps watching what someone else holds.
normalIntro.cn: envy 来自「看」：嫉妒的眼睛总盯着别人手里的东西。

normal.en: Green with envy is a common phrase for strong jealousy.
normal.cn: green with envy 是表示强烈嫉妒的常用短语。

normal.en: The envy of the street means the thing everyone wants.
normal.cn: the envy of the street 指人人想要的东西。

normal.en: Envious is the adjective, as in an envious glance.
normal.cn: envious 是形容词，如 an envious glance。

normal.en: Envy can be a noun or a verb without changing shape.
normal.cn: envy 可作名词也可作动词，词形不变。

normal.en: Compare jealousy: jealousy fears loss, envy wants another's good.
normal.cn: 对比 jealousy：jealousy 害怕失去，envy 渴望别人的好。

abstract.en: Picture an eye fixed on a fruit in another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼睛盯着别人手中的果子。

abstract.en: Imagine a green shadow falling over a smiling face.
abstract.cn: 想象一层绿色阴影落在一张笑脸上。

abstract.en: Think of a locked gate with a crowd gazing through.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门，一群人往里张望。

examples.en: He spoke of her promotion with open envy.
examples.cn: 他谈起她升职时毫不掩饰地流露出嫉妒。

examples.en: The little café is the envy of the neighborhood.
examples.cn: 这家小咖啡馆让整个街区羡慕。

examples.en: I envy her calm manner under pressure.
examples.cn: 我羡慕她在压力下的从容。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + vy」——看到别人的好就「眼红」，眼睛发绿；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（对着）＋ videre（看）→ invidere（带恶意地看）→ invidia（嫉妒）→ 古法语 envie → 英语 envy，核心义「看着别人的好而心生渴望」。

sensesIntro.en: Envy names the feeling, then the admired object, and finally the verb of feeling it toward someone.
sensesIntro.cn: envy 先指嫉妒的感受，再指被羡慕的对象，最后指对某人产生这种感受的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed gaze on something held by another.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光牢牢盯着别人手中的东西。

branches.en: The longing feeling is the central noun sense.
branches.cn: 渴望的感受是核心名词义项。

branches.en: The admired object is called the envy of others.
branches.cn: 被羡慕的对象被称为他人的 envy。

branches.en: The verb directs the feeling at a person.
branches.cn: 动词把这种感受指向某人。

branches.en: A thing becomes the envy of others because it stirs the feeling.
branches.cn: 某物之所以成为他人羡慕的对象，是因为它激起了这种感受。

branches.en: To envy someone is to carry the noun feeling into action.
branches.cn: 嫉妒某人，就是把名词的感受化为行动。

intro.en: Envy is a Latin seeing word, with English relatives envious and enviously and the same-root invidious.
intro.cn: envy 是拉丁语中与「看」有关的词，英语亲属有 envious、enviously 以及同根的 invidious。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre means to see, and invidere means to look at with ill will.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为看见，invidere 意为带着恶意看。

items.example: In- directs the look against someone.

items.exampleCN: invidere 把看与敌意结合起来。

items.example: Envie carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: envie 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Envy keeps both noun and verb uses.
items.exampleCN: envy 同时保留名词与动词用法。
enviously 描述某人看的方式。

definition_zh: 流行病；（坏事）迅速蔓延；流行性的
definition_en: a disease that spreads quickly through many people, or the rapid spread of something bad
core_image: 一条街接一条街，病人越来越多，像波纹扩散
scene: 那年冬天，流感在城里迅速蔓延。That winter, a flu epidemic swept through the city.
sceneCN: 这里 epidemic 是「流行病」（第 1 个义项：在人群中快速传播的疾病）；句意：那年冬天，流感在城里迅速蔓延。

senses.title: A quickly spreading disease
senses.definition: an infectious disease that spreads rapidly among many people in an area
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地区人群中迅速传播的传染病
senses.example: The city closed its schools during the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 疫情期间，这座城市关闭了学校。
senses.why: The Greek root means among the people, so a disease running through a whole population is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「在民众之中」，因此贯穿整个人群的疾病是第一个义项。

senses.title: The rapid spread of something bad
senses.definition: a rapid increase or spread of something harmful or unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 有害或不受欢迎之物的迅速增加或扩散
senses.example: Experts warn of an epidemic of online fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 专家警告网络诈骗正在迅速蔓延。
senses.why: The image of disease spreading is borrowed for any harmful trend.
senses.whyCN: 疾病传播的意象被借用来指任何有害趋势。

senses.title: Affecting many people at once
senses.definition: used as an adjective for something that spreads widely at one time
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词，指在某一时期广泛传播的事物
senses.example: Obesity has become an epidemic problem in many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 肥胖在许多国家已成为普遍性问题。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the same spreading idea and applies it to conditions or problems.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留同样的「扩散」概念，并用于状况或问题。

intro.en: Epidemic comes from Greek epidemos, among the people, from epi-, upon, and demos, the people.
intro.cn: epidemic 来自希腊语 epidemos（在民众之中），由 epi-（在上）与 demos（民众）构成。

items.en: Demos means the people.
items.cn: demos 意为民众。

items.en: Epi- means upon or among.
items.cn: epi- 意为在上或在……之中。

items.en: Epidemos means among the people.
items.cn: epidemos 意为在民众之中。

items.en: Epidemia names a disease visiting a whole population.
items.cn: epidemia 指降临整个人群的疾病。

items.en: French épidémie carries the medical sense.
items.cn: 法语 épidémie 保留医学含义。

items.en: Modern English extends epidemic to any rapid spread.
items.cn: 现代英语把 epidemic 扩展到任何迅速蔓延。

note.en: Epidemic is a spreading word from the demos family, near outbreak words and near its own technical relatives.
note.cn: epidemic 是来自 demos 词族的「扩散」词，与疫情词以及自身技术词族相邻。

entries.definition: the study of how diseases spread
regularly found in a particular place
a sudden start of disease or violence
a disease spreading across the world

normalIntro.en: Epidemic is epi- plus demos: a disease that settles upon the whole people.
normalIntro.cn: epidemic 是 epi- 加 demos：一种落到全体民众身上的疾病。

normal.en: Demos means people, and epidemic spreads among people.
normal.cn: demos 意为民众，epidemic 就在人群中传播。

normal.en: A flu epidemic sends many people to bed at once.
normal.cn: 流感流行会让许多人同时病倒。

normal.en: Epidemic proportions means a very large scale.
normal.cn: epidemic proportions 表示极大的规模。

normal.en: Epidemiology is the study of how epidemics move.
normal.cn: epidemiology 研究流行病如何传播。

normal.en: Compare endemic: endemic stays in one place, epidemic spreads.
normal.cn: 对比 endemic：endemic 局限一地，epidemic 会扩散。

abstract.en: Picture rings of illness widening street by street.
abstract.cn: 想象疾病像波纹一样一条街一条街地扩大。

abstract.en: Imagine a red dot spreading across a map of a city.
abstract.cn: 想象一个红点在城市地图上扩散。

abstract.en: Think of a rumor passing from door to door.
abstract.cn: 想象一则谣言从一扇门传到另一扇门。

examples.en: Doctors worked day and night to stop the epidemic.
examples.cn: 医生们日夜工作以阻止流行病蔓延。

examples.en: The report describes an epidemic of loneliness among the elderly.
examples.cn: 报告描述了老年人中普遍存在的孤独问题。

examples.en: Epidemic diseases spread fastest where people live close together.
examples.cn: 在人们居住密集的地方，流行性疾病传播得最快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「epi + demic」——疾病「压在」众人头上，就成了流行病；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ demos（民众）→ epidemos（在民众之中）→ epidemia（流行病）→ 英语 epidemic，核心义「在人群之中扩散」。

sensesIntro.en: Epidemic begins as a disease among the people, extends to any harmful spread, and then works as an adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: epidemic 从人群中的疾病开始，扩展到任何有害的蔓延，再作形容词使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: illness moving through a whole population.
core.cn: 核心意象：疾病穿过整个人群。

branches.en: A spreading disease is the original medical sense.
branches.cn: 传播中的疾病是最初的医学义项。

branches.en: Any harmful spread borrows the disease image.
branches.cn: 任何有害蔓延都借用了疾病的意象。

branches.en: The adjective describes what affects many at once.
branches.cn: 形容词描述同时影响许多人的事物。

branches.en: Both a virus and a fraud wave move quickly through crowds.
branches.cn: 病毒与诈骗浪潮都在人群中快速移动。

branches.en: A disease becomes epidemic when it reaches many people.
branches.cn: 疾病在波及许多人时成为流行性的。

intro.en: Epidemic is built from Greek epi- and demos, with a large English family in epidemiology and its forms.
intro.cn: epidemic 由希腊语 epi- 与 demos 构成，英语词族在 epidemiology 及其派生词中扩展。

latinIntro.en: Greek epi- means upon, and demos means the people.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 epi- 意为在上，demos 意为民众。

items.example: Epi- places the disease upon the people.
items.exampleCN: epi- 把疾病置于民众之上。
epidemos 把两部分组合起来。

items.example: Epidemia is the Greek medical noun.
items.exampleCN: epidemia 是希腊语医学名词。
epidemiology 研究疾病如何传播。

definition_en: one part of a series, or a single event in a longer story
core_image: 一条长线被分成几段，每段都有自己的开头和结尾
scene: 这部纪录片的第三集讲的是深海生物。The third episode of the documentary looks at deep-sea life.
sceneCN: 这里 episode 是「一集」（第 1 个义项：系列节目中的一个部分）；句意：这部纪录片的第三集讲的是深海生物。

senses.title: One part of a series
senses.definition: one program in a television or radio series
senses.definitionCN: 电视或广播系列节目中的一期
senses.example: The final episode answered every question.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一集回答了所有疑问。
senses.why: Greek epeisodion meant an interlude between choral songs, and a single part of a series keeps that sense of a bounded section.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 epeisodion 指合唱之间的插段，系列中的一个部分保留了「有边界的段落」这一含义。

senses.title: A single event in a longer story
senses.definition: one event or period within a longer series of events
senses.definitionCN: 较长事件序列中的一个事件或时期
senses.example: That summer was a strange episode in his life.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天是他人生中一段奇怪的经历。
senses.why: A bounded section of a story becomes a bounded event in a life.
senses.whyCN: 故事中有边界的一段，变成人生中有边界的一个事件。

senses.title: A period of illness
senses.definition: a short period when a disease or condition is active
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或症状活跃的一段短时期
senses.example: She had a brief episode of dizziness.
senses.exampleCN: 她有过一小段眩晕发作。
senses.why: Medical use treats a bout of illness as a separate section of time.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把一次病情发作视为一段独立的时间。

intro.en: Episode comes from Greek epeisodion, an addition or interlude, from epi-, upon, and eisodos, a coming in.
intro.cn: episode 来自希腊语 epeisodion（附加段、插曲），由 epi-（在上）与 eisodos（进入）构成。

items.en: Eisodos means a coming in or entrance.
items.cn: eisodos 意为进入、入场。

items.en: Epeisodion means an added interlude.
items.cn: epeisodion 意为附加的插段。

items.en: The word names a section between choral songs.
items.cn: 这个词指合唱歌曲之间的段落。

items.en: French épisode applies it to a part of a story.
items.cn: 法语 épisode 把它用于故事的一部分。

items.en: Modern English uses episode for series parts, events, and bouts of illness.
items.cn: 现代英语用 episode 指剧集、事件和病情发作。

note.en: Episode is a section word, linked to episodic forms and to words for parts of a whole.
note.cn: episode 是表示「段落」的词，与 episodic 词族以及表示整体之部分的词相邻。

entries.definition: one part of a story released in stages
a main division of a book

normalIntro.en: Episode is a self-contained section: a show part, a life event, or a bout of illness.
normalIntro.cn: episode 是一个自成一体的段落：一集节目、一段人生经历，或一次病情发作。

normal.en: A TV series is made of episodes.
normal.cn: 电视剧由一集一集的 episode 组成。

normal.en: The first episode introduces the main characters.
normal.cn: 第一集介绍主要人物。

normal.en: A brief episode of rain passed quickly.
normal.cn: 一阵短暂的降雨很快过去了。

normal.en: The adjective episodic means made of separate parts.
normal.cn: 形容词 episodic 意为由分开的部分组成。

normal.en: Compare chapter: chapter is for books, episode suits shows and events.
normal.cn: 对比 chapter：chapter 用于书，episode 适用于节目和事件。

abstract.en: Picture a long ribbon cut into neat sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长丝带被剪成整齐的几段。

abstract.en: Imagine a door opening onto one scene and closing again.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门打开呈现一幕，然后又关上。

abstract.en: Think of a short storm passing over a calm sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一场短促的暴风雨掠过平静的海面。

examples.en: We watched the opening episode together.
examples.cn: 我们一起看了开篇那一集。

examples.en: The trip was a happy episode in her childhood.
examples.cn: 那次旅行是她童年中一段快乐的经历。

examples.en: He described a sudden episode of back pain.
examples.cn: 他描述了一次突然发作的背痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「epi + sode」——一段插进来的小故事，就是一集；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上）＋ eisodos（进入）→ epeisodion（插段）→ 法语 épisode → 英语 episode，核心义「整体中的一个段落」。

sensesIntro.en: Episode starts as an interlude, then becomes one part of a series, a single life event, and a bout of illness.
sensesIntro.cn: episode 从插段开始，随后指系列中的一集、人生中的一个事件，以及一次病情发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long line divided into bounded sections.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长线被分成有边界的段落。

branches.en: One part of a series is the everyday media sense.
branches.cn: 系列中的一集是日常媒体义项。

branches.en: A single event is a section of a life story.
branches.cn: 单个事件是人生故事中的一个段落。

branches.en: A bout of illness is a bounded period of time.
branches.cn: 病情发作是一段有边界的时间。

branches.en: Both a show part and a life event have a clear beginning and end.
branches.cn: 一集节目与一段经历都有清楚的起点和终点。

branches.en: An illness episode is also an event in a person's history.
branches.cn: 一次发病也是个人经历中的一个事件。

intro.en: Episode comes from Greek roots, and English adds the adjective and adverb endings -ic and -ally.
intro.cn: episode 来自希腊语词根，英语再加上形容词与副词词尾 -ic 和 -ally。

latinIntro.en: Greek epi- means upon, and eisodos means a coming in.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 epi- 意为在上，eisodos 意为进入。

items.example: Episodically means from time to time.

definition_zh: 相等的；平等的；同等的人；等于
definition_en: the same in amount, value, or status, or to be the same as something
core_image: 天平两端放着同样重的东西，横杆保持水平
scene: 两根绳子长度相同，承受的重量也一样。The two ropes are equal in length and strength.
sceneCN: 这里 equal 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上相同）；句意：两根绳子的长度和强度都相同。

senses.title: The same in amount or degree
senses.definition: having the same size, amount, value, or level as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量、价值或水平上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: Cut the cake into eight equal pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 把蛋糕切成八块大小相等的份。
senses.why: Latin aequalis means level or even, so equal first describes things that balance perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequalis 意为水平、均匀，所以 equal 首先描述完全平衡的事物。

senses.title: Having the same rights or status
senses.definition: having the same rights, opportunities, or treatment as others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他人拥有相同的权利、机会或待遇
senses.example: Every citizen deserves equal treatment under the law.
senses.exampleCN: 每位公民在法律面前都应得到平等对待。
senses.why: The idea of an even balance extends from weights and amounts to people and their rights.
senses.whyCN: 「平衡」的概念从重量和数量扩展到人及其权利。

senses.title: A person of the same rank
senses.definition: a person who has the same ability, rank, or status as another
senses.definitionCN: 能力、地位或身份与另一人相同的人
senses.example: She treats her students as her equals.
senses.exampleCN: 她把学生当作与自己平等的人。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for someone who stands on the same level.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指站在同一水平上的人。

senses.title: To be the same as
senses.definition: to be the same in amount or value as something, or to match it
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或价值上等同于某物，或与之匹敌
senses.example: Two plus three equals five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: The verb turns the balanced relation into an action of matching.
senses.whyCN: 动词把平衡关系转化为「相配、等同」的动作。

intro.en: Equal comes from Latin aequalis, uniform or even, from aequus, level or fair.
intro.cn: equal 来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀、相等），源于 aequus（平的、公平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level, even, or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均匀的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means uniform or of the same age.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的或同年的。

items.en: Equal carries the sense of even and alike.
items.cn: equal 带有「平、相同」的含义。

items.en: Equal covers amounts and the rights of people.
items.cn: 中古英语 equal 涵盖数量与人的权利。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun for a person of the same rank.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示同等之人的名词用法。

note.en: Equal is a balance word with a large family and a set of near words for sameness.
note.cn: equal 是表示「平衡」的词，拥有庞大词族，并与表示相同的一组词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Equal comes from a level root: two sides of a scale sitting perfectly even.
normalIntro.cn: equal 来自「水平」的词根：天平两边完全齐平。

normal.en: Equal parts means every part is the same size.
normal.cn: equal parts 指每一份大小相同。

normal.en: Equal rights means the same rights for everyone.
normal.cn: equal rights 指人人拥有相同权利。

normal.en: The verb equals appears in arithmetic.
normal.cn: 动词 equals 出现在算术中。

normal.en: Equality is the noun for the equal state.
normal.cn: equality 是表示平等状态的名词。

normal.en: Compare identical: identical is stricter, equal allows different forms of the same value.
normal.cn: 对比 identical：identical 更严格，equal 允许同一价值的不同形式。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with two identical weights.
abstract.cn: 想象一台天平两端放着相同的砝码。

abstract.en: Imagine eight cake slices cut by a careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手仔细切出八块相同的蛋糕。

abstract.en: Think of two runners crossing a line at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者同时冲过终点线。

examples.en: The two teams finished with equal scores.
examples.cn: 两支队伍最终得分相同。

examples.en: The law promises equal pay for equal work.
examples.cn: 法律承诺同工同酬。

examples.en: One kilometer equals a thousand meters.
examples.cn: 一公里等于一千米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + qual」——两边一样平，就是相等；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的、公平的）→ aequalis（均匀的）→ 古法语 equal → 英语 equal，核心义「两端齐平、彼此相同」。

sensesIntro.en: Equal starts with even amounts, extends to fair treatment, then to a person of the same standing, and finally to the verb of matching.
sensesIntro.cn: equal 从数量相等开始，扩展到公平对待，再指地位相同的人，最后成为表示「等于」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale perfectly level on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两边完全水平。

branches.en: Even amount is the basic measurable sense.
branches.cn: 数量相等是基本的可测量义项。

branches.en: Fair treatment extends balance to rights.
branches.cn: 公平对待把平衡扩展到权利。

branches.en: A peer is a person on the same level.
branches.cn: 同等之人是站在同一水平上的人。

branches.en: The verb states that two things match.
branches.cn: 动词陈述两事物彼此相等。

branches.en: Equal shares and equal rights both rest on the same balance.
branches.cn: 均分与平权都建立在同一种平衡之上。

intro.en: Equal is a Latin fairness word, and English builds equality, equally, and equate around it.
intro.cn: equal 是拉丁语中表示公平的词，英语围绕它构成 equality、equally 与 equate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level and fair, and aequalis means even or uniform.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的、公平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

items.example: Equally means in the same measure.

items.exampleCN: un- 在 unequal 中否定 equal。

definition_en: the state of being equal in rights, status, or amount
core_image: 天平两端准确齐平，谁也不少一分
scene: 法律保证男女在就业上享有平等。The law guarantees equality between men and women at work.
sceneCN: 这里 equality 是「平等」（第 1 个义项：在权利或地位上相同）；句意：法律保证男女在就业上享有平等。

senses.title: Equal rights and status
senses.definition: the state in which people have the same rights, opportunities, and respect
senses.definitionCN: 人们拥有相同权利、机会与尊重的情形
senses.example: The movement fought for equality in education.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动为教育平等而斗争。
senses.why: The noun adds -ity to equal, naming the state of being level and fair.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 equal 加 -ity 构成，指齐平而公平的状态。

senses.title: Equality in amount or value
senses.definition: the condition of being the same in size, amount, or value
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或价值上相同的状况
senses.example: The treaty rests on the equality of the two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约建立在双方对等的基础上。
senses.why: Before it meant fair treatment, the word simply named an even balance.
senses.whyCN: 在表示公平对待之前，这个词只表示均衡。

senses.title: Evenness of treatment
senses.definition: the quality of treating all cases by the same standard
senses.definitionCN: 以同一标准对待所有情况的品质
senses.example: Judges must show equality to every citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 法官必须对每位公民一视同仁。
senses.why: A level balance in practice becomes consistent and impartial treatment.
senses.whyCN: 均衡在实际中表现为一致而公正的对待。

intro.en: Equality comes from Latin aequalitas, evenness, from aequalis, equal, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equality 来自拉丁语 aequalitas（均匀、相等），源于 aequalis（相等的）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means uniform or equal.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的、相等的。

items.en: Aequalitas names the state of being equal.
items.cn: aequalitas 指相等的状态。

items.en: Equal brings the adjective into French and English.
items.cn: equal 把这个形容词带入法语和英语。

items.en: Modern English adds -ity to form the noun equality.
items.cn: 现代英语加 -ity 构成名词 equality。

note.en: Equality is the state noun of equal, close to its family and to words for fairness.
note.cn: equality 是 equal 的状态名词，与自身词族以及表示公平的词相邻。

entries.definition: the same in amount or status
the state of being equal in rank
fairness in the way people are treated

normalIntro.en: Equality is the state of the equal: a level scale applied to people and to numbers.
normalIntro.cn: equality 是 equal 的状态：把水平的天平用于人与数字。

normal.en: Gender equality means equal chances for women and men.
normal.cn: gender equality 指男女机会平等。

normal.en: Equality before the law means the law treats everyone alike.
normal.cn: equality before the law 指法律对人人一视同仁。

normal.en: The adjective equal and the noun equality differ by only a suffix.
normal.cn: 形容词 equal 与名词 equality 只差一个词尾。

normal.en: Equality of opportunity is a common political phrase.
normal.cn: equality of opportunity 是常见的政治短语。

normal.en: Compare fairness: fairness stresses justice, equality stresses sameness.
normal.cn: 对比 fairness：fairness 强调公正，equality 强调相同。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with both pans at the very same height.
abstract.cn: 想象天平的托盘处在完全相同的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine two doors of exactly the same width.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇宽度完全相同的门。

abstract.en: Think of a line drawn straight through the middle of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象页面正中画着一条笔直的线。

examples.en: They marched for equality and justice.
examples.cn: 他们为平等与正义而游行。

examples.en: True equality means the same rules for everyone.
examples.cn: 真正的平等意味着人人适用同样的规则。

examples.en: The two countries agreed on the equality of their trade rights.
examples.cn: 两国就贸易权利对等达成一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal + ity」——给「相等」加上状态名词尾巴，就是「平等」；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的、公平的）→ aequalis（相等的）→ aequalitas（相等状态）→ 英语 equality，核心义「彼此齐平的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Equality first names fair rights, then an even balance of amount, and then consistent treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: equality 先指公平权利，再指数额上的均衡，最后指一致对待。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale whose two sides sit at the same height.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两边处在同一高度。

branches.en: Fair rights are the central social sense.
branches.cn: 公平权利是核心社会义项。

branches.en: Even amount is the measurable sense.
branches.cn: 数额相等是可测量的义项。

branches.en: Consistent treatment applies balance to practice.
branches.cn: 一致对待把平衡用于实践。

branches.en: Equal rights require the same standard for all.
branches.cn: 平等权利要求对所有人使用同一标准。

branches.en: Both fair shares and fair rights rest on an even balance.
branches.cn: 公平分配与公平权利都建立在均衡之上。

intro.en: Equality is a Latin state noun built on aequus, with the suffix -ity added in English.
intro.cn: equality 是建立在 aequus 之上的拉丁状态名词，英语中加入词尾 -ity。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, and aequalitas means evenness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequalitas 意为均匀、相等。

items.example: Aequalitas is the direct Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: aequalitas 是直接的拉丁语名词。

definition_en: in an equal way, or to the same degree
core_image: 两杯水被倒到完全相同的高度
scene: 把奖金平均分给四个孩子。Divide the prize money equally among the four children.
sceneCN: 这里 equally 是「均等地」（第 1 个义项：以相同的份额或数量）；句意：把奖金平均分给四个孩子。

senses.title: In equal shares
senses.definition: in the same amount or share for each person or part
senses.definitionCN: 给每个人或每一部分相同的数量或份额
senses.example: The money was shared equally between the two sisters.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔钱在两姐妹之间平均分配。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to equal, so it describes an action done in an even way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 equal 加 -ly 构成，描述以均衡方式完成的动作。

senses.title: To the same degree
senses.definition: to the same degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 达到相同的程度或范围
senses.example: Both plans are equally risky.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案的风险同样大。
senses.why: The balance sense extends from shares to degrees of a quality.
senses.whyCN: 「份额均衡」的概念扩展到某种品质的程度。

senses.title: Used to add a matching point
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to add a point of the same weight
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，补充一个分量相同的观点
senses.example: Equally, we must consider the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 同样，我们也必须考虑成本。
senses.why: If two points weigh the same, the second can be introduced as equally important.
senses.whyCN: 如果两个观点分量相同，第二个就可以作为同样重要的一点引出。

intro.en: Equally is equal plus -ly, from Latin aequalis, even, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equally 是 equal 加 -ly，来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀的）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means even or equal.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的、相等的。

items.en: Equal enters English as an adjective.
items.cn: equal 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly forms the adverb equally.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 equally。

items.en: Equally also introduces a second point of the same weight.
items.cn: 现代英语中，equally 也用于引出第二个同等分量的观点。

note.en: Equally is the adverb of equal, near its family and near adverbs for sameness.
note.cn: equally 是 equal 的副词，与自身词族以及表示相同的副词相邻。

entries.definition: in an even or balanced way

normalIntro.en: Equally is equal plus -ly: whatever is equal is done or measured in an equal way.
normalIntro.cn: equally 是 equal 加 -ly：相等的东西，就以相等的方式去做或衡量。

normal.en: Divide equally means give everyone the same share.
normal.cn: divide equally 指给每个人相同的一份。

normal.en: Equally important means just as important.
normal.cn: equally important 表示同样重要。

normal.en: Equally spaced dots sit the same distance apart.
normal.cn: equally spaced 的点彼此距离相同。

normal.en: Equally at the start of a sentence adds a matching point.
normal.cn: equally 放在句首，补充一个对等的观点。

normal.en: Compare evenly: evenly stresses smooth distribution, equally stresses sameness.
normal.cn: 对比 evenly：evenly 强调分布平滑，equally 强调相同。

abstract.en: Picture two glasses filled to exactly the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象两只杯子被倒到完全相同的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a row of trees planted at identical gaps.
abstract.cn: 想象一排树以相同间距种下。

abstract.en: Think of two weights resting level on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两个砝码在天平上保持水平。

examples.en: The estate was divided equally among the three children.
examples.cn: 遗产在三个孩子之间平均分配。

examples.en: Both candidates are equally qualified for the job.
examples.cn: 两位候选人都同样胜任这份工作。

examples.en: Equally, we should ask who pays for the repairs.
examples.cn: 同样，我们也应该问清谁来支付维修费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal + ly」——用「相等」的方式去做，就是同样地；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的）→ aequalis（相等的）→ 英语 equal ＋ -ly → equally，核心义「以相同的方式或程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Equally starts with equal shares, extends to equal degrees, and is then used to add a point of the same weight.
sensesIntro.cn: equally 从均分开始，扩展到相同程度，随后用于补充同等分量的观点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two containers filled to the same level.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个容器被装到同一高度。

branches.en: Equal shares are the basic distributive sense.
branches.cn: 均分是基本的分配义项。

branches.en: Equal degree extends balance to qualities.
branches.cn: 同等程度把平衡扩展到品质。

branches.en: Adding a matching point uses equal weight in argument.
branches.cn: 补充对等观点，是在论证中使用同等分量。

branches.en: A fair share and an equal degree both rest on the same measure.
branches.cn: 公平份额与相同程度都建立在同一尺度上。

branches.en: Two equally strong points can both be introduced with equally.
branches.cn: 两个同样有力的观点都可以用 equally 引出。

intro.en: Equally is a Latin balance adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: equally 是拉丁语「平衡」形容词加上英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, and aequalis means even.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

items.example: Equally means by the same measure.

definition_en: a mathematical statement that two things are equal, or a set of factors to balance
core_image: 等号两边放着同样多的东西，必须保持平衡
scene: 老师让学生在黑板上解一道简单的方程。The teacher asked a student to solve a simple equation on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 equation 是「方程式」（第 1 个义项：数学中用等号连接两边的式子）；句意：老师让学生在黑板上解一道简单的方程。

collocations.phrase: the other side of the equation

senses.title: A mathematical equation
senses.definition: a mathematical statement showing that two expressions are equal
senses.definitionCN: 表明两个表达式相等的数学陈述
senses.example: This equation has two possible answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有两个可能的解。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to make equal, so it names a statement of equality.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自意为「使相等」的拉丁动词，因此指一个表示相等的陈述。

senses.title: A chemical equation
senses.definition: a symbolic statement that balances the atoms on each side of a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 用符号表示反应两边原子数平衡的式子
senses.example: The class balanced the chemical equation together.
senses.exampleCN: 全班一起配平了这个化学方程式。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the equal-sign form to show that matter is conserved.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用等号形式来表示物质守恒。

senses.title: A set of factors to balance
senses.titleCN: 复杂局面；需权衡的因素
senses.definition: a situation in which several factors must be weighed together
senses.definitionCN: 必须把多个因素放在一起权衡的情形
senses.example: Cost is only one part of the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 成本只是需要权衡的因素之一。
senses.why: If an equation balances two sides, a real situation can be pictured as sides to weigh.
senses.whyCN: 如果方程要平衡两边，现实局面也可以被想象成需要权衡的两边。

intro.en: Equation comes from Latin aequatio, a making equal, from aequare, to make level, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equation 来自拉丁语 aequatio（使相等），源于 aequare（使平）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequare means to make equal or level.
items.cn: aequare 意为使相等、使平。

items.en: Aequatio names the act of making equal.
items.cn: aequatio 指使相等的动作。

items.en: Équation applies the word to algebra.
items.cn: 法语 équation 把这个词用于代数。

items.en: Modern English extends equation to chemistry and to mixed situations.
items.cn: 现代英语把 equation 扩展到化学与复杂局面。

note.en: Equation is a balance word from the aequus family, close to formula and expression.
note.cn: equation 是来自 aequus 词族的「平衡」词，与 formula 和 expression 相邻。

entries.definition: a rule or relationship written in symbols
an equation true for all values

normalIntro.en: Equation is a little balance: whatever is on one side of the equal sign must match the other.
normalIntro.cn: equation 是一架小天平：等号一边的东西必须与另一边相配。

normal.en: To solve an equation is to find the value that keeps both sides equal.
normal.cn: 解方程就是找出让两边保持相等的值。

normal.en: A linear equation draws a straight line on a graph.
normal.cn: 线性方程在图上画出一条直线。

normal.en: A chemical equation must be balanced atom by atom.
normal.cn: 化学方程式必须逐个原子配平。

normal.en: The other side of the equation means the factors you forgot.
normal.cn: 「the other side of the equation」指你忽略的另一面因素。

normal.en: Compare formula: a formula is a rule, an equation states equality.
normal.cn: 对比 formula：formula 是规则，equation 陈述相等关系。

abstract.en: Picture an equal sign holding two trays level.
abstract.cn: 想象一个等号托着两只水平的托盘。

abstract.en: Imagine atoms counted carefully on both sides of an arrow.
abstract.cn: 想象箭头两边被仔细数过的原子。

abstract.en: Think of a scale where cost sits on one pan and benefit on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一边是成本，一边是收益。

examples.en: She solved the equation in her head.
examples.cn: 她心算解出了这个方程。

examples.en: Every chemical equation must balance.
examples.cn: 每个化学方程式都必须配平。

examples.en: Time is the missing factor in the equation.
examples.cn: 时间是这一局面中缺失的因素。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equ + ation」——把两边「弄成一样」，就是方程式；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的）→ aequare（使相等）→ aequatio（使相等）→ 法语 équation → 英语 equation，核心义「两边相等的陈述」。

sensesIntro.en: Equation begins as a statement of mathematical equality, extends to chemistry, and then to any set of factors to balance.
sensesIntro.cn: equation 从数学上的相等陈述开始，扩展到化学，再扩展到任何需要权衡的因素组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides of an equal sign held in balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：等号两边保持平衡。

branches.en: The mathematical statement is the core sense.
branches.cn: 数学陈述是核心义项。

branches.en: Chemistry applies the equal-sign form to atoms.
branches.cn: 化学把等号形式用于原子。

branches.en: A real situation becomes sides that must be weighed.
branches.cn: 现实局面变成需要权衡的两边。

branches.en: Both a math equation and a hard choice involve balancing sides.
branches.cn: 数学方程与艰难选择都涉及平衡两边。

branches.en: Both math and chemistry equations must stay balanced.
branches.cn: 数学方程与化学方程式都必须保持平衡。

intro.en: Equation is a Latin noun of making equal, and English builds equate and equational around the same root.
intro.cn: equation 是拉丁语中表示「使相等」的名词，英语围绕同一词根构成 equate 与 equational。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means level, aequare means to make equal, and aequatio means a making equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequare 意为使相等，aequatio 意为使相等的过程。

definition_en: to supply someone or something with the tools or skills needed
core_image: 出发前把工具一件件装进背包
scene: 学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。The school equipped every lab with new microscopes.
sceneCN: 这里 equipped 是 equip 的过去式，表示「配备」（第 1 个义项：提供所需的工具或设备）；句意：学校为每间实验室配备了新的显微镜。

senses.title: To supply with tools or gear
senses.definition: to provide a person or place with the tools, machines, or gear needed
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需的工具、机器或装备
senses.example: The team was equipped with maps and radios.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍配备了地图和无线电。
senses.why: The word came from fitting out a ship, so the basic sense is supplying the necessary gear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指为船只配备物资，因此基本含义是提供必需的装备。

senses.title: To prepare someone with skills
senses.definition: to give someone the knowledge or skills needed for a task
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人完成任务所需的知识或技能
senses.example: The course equips students to work in hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程使学生有能力在医院工作。
senses.why: Equipment can be mental as well as physical, so the verb extends to training.
senses.whyCN: 装备既可以是物质的，也可以是头脑中的，所以动词扩展到培训。

senses.title: To fit out a place
senses.definition: to furnish a room, building, or vehicle with what it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为房间、建筑或车辆配置所需设备
senses.example: They equipped the new kitchen with modern appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为新厨房配置了现代电器。
senses.why: The same supplying action applies to places and vehicles, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 同样的供给动作也适用于场所和车辆，而不只是人。

intro.en: Equip comes from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic word for ship.
intro.cn: equip 来自古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资），可能源于日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 一词意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备物资。

items.en: The word extends to fitting out a person or army.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到为个人或军队配备。

items.en: Equip enters English with the gear sense.
items.cn: equip 以「装备」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of preparing with skills.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「以技能作准备」的含义。

note.en: Equip is a supplying verb, closely tied to equipment and to words for furnishing.
note.cn: equip 是表示供给的动词，与 equipment 以及表示配置的词关系紧密。

entries.definition: to supply a room with furniture

normalIntro.en: Equip began as fitting out a ship; now you can equip a lab, a team, or a student.
normalIntro.cn: equip 最初指为船只配备物资；现在可以为实验室、队伍或学生配备所需。

normal.en: Equip with means supply with.
normal.cn: equip with 表示配备。

normal.en: A fully equipped kitchen has every tool you need.
normal.cn: fully equipped 的厨房拥有你需要的每样工具。

normal.en: The noun equipment is uncountable.
normal.cn: 名词 equipment 是不可数名词。

normal.en: A course can equip you for a career.
normal.cn: 一门课程可以让你有能力从事某种职业。

normal.en: Compare supply: supply is broader, equip stresses gear or preparation.
normal.cn: 对比 supply：supply 更宽泛，equip 强调装备或准备。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor loading ropes and lanterns onto a ship.
abstract.cn: 想象水手把绳索和灯笼装上船。

abstract.en: Imagine a hiker checking each item in a backpack.
abstract.cn: 想象徒步者逐一检查背包里的物品。

abstract.en: Think of a student leaving a class with a new skill.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生带着新技能走出课堂。

examples.en: Rescue teams were equipped with warm clothing.
examples.cn: 救援队配备了保暖衣物。

examples.en: The training equips nurses to handle emergencies.
examples.cn: 这项培训使护士有能力处理紧急情况。

examples.en: They equipped the office with new computers.
examples.cn: 他们为办公室配备了新电脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + quip」——出发前把工具「配齐」，就是装备；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资）→ 中古英语 equip，核心义「把所需之物配齐」，引申为使有能力。

sensesIntro.en: Equip starts with supplying gear, extends to preparing people with skills, and applies to fitting out places.
sensesIntro.cn: equip 从提供装备开始，扩展到以技能培养人，并适用于为场所配置设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a backpack filled with every tool the trip needs.
core.cn: 核心意象：背包里装满旅途所需的每样工具。

branches.en: Supplying tools is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 提供工具是基本的物质义项。

branches.en: Supplying skills extends gear to the mind.
branches.cn: 提供技能把装备扩展到头脑。

branches.en: Fitting out a place applies the same action to rooms.
branches.cn: 为场所配置设备把同一动作用于房间。

branches.en: A lab and a hiker are both fitted out with gear.
branches.cn: 实验室与徒步者都被配齐了装备。

branches.en: Both tools and training prepare someone for a task.
branches.cn: 工具与培训都让人为任务做好准备。

intro.en: Equip is a French fitting-out verb, with English equipment and equipped built from it.
intro.cn: equip 是法语中表示「配备」的动词，英语由它构成 equipment 与 equipped。

latinIntro.en: The French esquiper, to fit out a ship, probably comes from a Germanic word for ship.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 esquiper（为船只配备）可能来自日耳曼语中表示「船」的词。

items.example: Skip is the probable ship root.
items.exampleCN: skip 是可能表示「船」的词根。

items.example: Esquiper starts as a sailing word.

items.meaning: forming a past form or adjective

items.exampleCN: equipped 描述准备好的状态。
equipping 指正在进行的动作。
fully 常与 equipped 搭配。

definition_en: the tools, machines, or gear needed for a particular purpose
core_image: 一堆工具整齐摆开，随时可以带上出发
scene: 登山前，队员检查了所有装备。Before the climb, the team checked all their equipment.
sceneCN: 这里 equipment 是「装备」（第 1 个义项：为特定目的所需的工具和器材）；句意：登山前，队员检查了所有装备。

senses.title: Tools and machines for a purpose
senses.definition: the set of tools or machines used for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的整套工具或机器
senses.example: The lab bought new equipment for the students.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为学生购买了新设备。
senses.why: The noun adds -ment to equip, naming all the things supplied rather than the act of supplying.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 equip 加 -ment 构成，指被配备的全部物品，而不是配备的动作。

senses.title: Special gear for an activity
senses.definition: the clothing or gear needed for a sport, job, or journey
senses.definitionCN: 运动、工作或旅行所需的服装或装备
senses.example: Climbing equipment must be checked before every trip.
senses.exampleCN: 每次出行前都必须检查登山装备。
senses.why: Equipment can be personal gear as well as shared machines.
senses.whyCN: equipment 既可以是共用机器，也可以是个人装备。

senses.title: The act of fitting out
senses.definition: the process of supplying a person or place with what is needed, used in formal contexts
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某地提供所需之物的过程，用于正式语境
senses.example: The equipment of the new hospital took a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 新医院的设备配置花了整整一年。
senses.why: The suffix -ment can name an action as well as its result, which keeps the older process sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ment 既可指动作也可指结果，因此保留了较老的「过程」含义。

intro.en: Equipment is equip plus -ment, from Old French esquiper, to fit out a ship.
intro.cn: equipment 是 equip 加 -ment，源自法语 esquiper（为船只配备物资）。

items.en: A Germanic skip word means ship.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中 skip 意为船。

items.en: Esquiper means to fit out a ship.
items.cn: esquiper 意为为船只配备。

items.en: Equip enters English as a verb.
items.cn: equip 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ment forms the noun equipment.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 构成名词 equipment。

items.en: Equipment covers tools for work, sport, and medicine.
items.cn: 现代英语中，equipment 涵盖工作、运动和医疗器材。

note.en: Equipment is the noun of equip, close to its verb and adjective and to words for gear.
note.cn: equipment 是 equip 的名词，与它的动词、形容词形式以及表示「装备」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a set of equipment or a carriage
the equipment needed for an activity
a set of equipment for a purpose

normalIntro.en: Equipment is what equip supplies: the whole set of tools and gear.
normalIntro.cn: equipment 就是 equip 提供的东西：整套工具与装备。

normal.en: Equipment is uncountable, so say a piece of equipment.
normal.cn: equipment 不可数，所以说 a piece of equipment。

normal.en: Safety equipment protects workers.
normal.cn: safety equipment 保护工人。

normal.en: Medical equipment must be kept clean.
normal.cn: medical equipment 必须保持清洁。

normal.en: Heavy equipment moves earth and stone.
normal.cn: heavy equipment 用来移动土石。

normal.en: Compare gear: gear is more informal, equipment is broader and formal.
normal.cn: 对比 gear：gear 更口语，equipment 更宽泛正式。

abstract.en: Picture a neat row of tools laid out before a job.
abstract.cn: 想象干活前整齐摆开的一排工具。

abstract.en: Imagine a climber counting ropes and clips by a tent.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在帐篷旁清点绳索和锁扣。

abstract.en: Think of a hospital room filled with humming machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一间充满机器低鸣的医院病房。

examples.en: All equipment must be stored in a dry room.
examples.cn: 所有设备都必须存放在干燥的房间里。

examples.en: She packed her camera equipment into two bags.
examples.cn: 她把摄影器材装进了两个包。

examples.en: The school spent a large sum on sports equipment.
examples.cn: 学校在体育器材上花了一大笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equip + ment」——被「配齐」的那些东西，就是设备；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 esquiper（为船只配备）→ 英语 equip（装备）＋ -ment → equipment，核心义「被配备起来的一整套用具」。

sensesIntro.en: Equipment first means the tools supplied, then personal gear, and in formal use the process of fitting out.
sensesIntro.cn: equipment 先指被提供的工具，再指个人装备，在正式用法中还指配置过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full set of tools laid out and ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整套工具摆放齐全待用。

branches.en: The tool set is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 整套工具是现代主要义项。

branches.en: Personal gear is a narrower use.
branches.cn: 个人装备是较窄的用法。

branches.en: Fitting out keeps the older process sense.
branches.cn: 配置过程保留较老的过程含义。

branches.en: Both a lab machine and a climbing rope are supplied gear.
branches.cn: 实验室机器与登山绳都是被配备的装备。

branches.en: The equipment of a place is the result of equipping it.
branches.cn: 一个场所的设备是配置过程的结果。

intro.en: Equipment is equip with -ment, and it shares the fitting-out root with the verb.
intro.cn: equipment 是 equip 加 -ment，与动词共享「配备」词根。

latinIntro.en: Old French esquiper means to fit out a ship, probably from a Germanic ship word.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 esquiper 意为为船只配备，可能来自日耳曼语表示船的单词。

items.example: Gear is the informal near word.

definition_en: equal in value, meaning, or effect, or something that matches another
core_image: 两枚不同的硬币放在天平上，重量正好相同
scene: 一英里大约相当于一点六公里。One mile is roughly equivalent to one point six kilometers.
sceneCN: 这里 equivalent 是「相等的」（第 1 个义项：在价值、数量或意义上相同）；句意：一英里大约等于一点六公里。

senses.title: Equal in value or amount
senses.definition: having the same value, amount, or meaning as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在价值、数量或意义上与他人或他物相同
senses.example: A dollar is not equivalent to a euro.
senses.exampleCN: 一美元并不等于一欧元。
senses.why: Latin aequus means equal and valere means be worth, so equivalent literally means worth the same.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aequus 意为相等，valere 意为值，因此 equivalent 字面意思就是「价值相同」。

senses.title: Equal in effect or role
senses.definition: having the same result, function, or force as something else
senses.definitionCN: 产生相同结果、功能或效力的
senses.example: Silence was equivalent to agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默等同于同意。
senses.why: If two things are worth the same, they can stand in for each other in effect.
senses.whyCN: 如果两物价值相同，它们在效果上就可以互相替代。

senses.title: A matching thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that has the same value or role as another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或物具有相同价值或角色的人或物
senses.example: This word has no exact equivalent in English.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在英语中没有完全对应的说法。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the matching item itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指与之匹配的事物本身。

intro.en: Equivalent joins Latin aequus, equal, and valere, to be worth, so it means having equal worth.
intro.cn: equivalent 结合拉丁语 aequus（相等的）与 valere（值），意为具有相同的价值。

items.en: Aequus means equal or level.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等的、平的。

items.en: Valere means to be worth or be strong.
items.cn: valere 意为值、有力量。

items.en: Aequivalere means to be worth the same.
items.cn: aequivalere 意为价值相等。

items.en: Aequivalentem is the present participle form.
items.cn: aequivalentem 是现在分词形式。

items.en: Équivalent carries the word into French.
items.cn: équivalent 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Modern English uses equivalent as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 现代英语中 equivalent 兼作形容词与名词。

note.en: Equivalent is a worth-matching word, close to its family and to words for comparability.
note.cn: equivalent 是表示「价值相配」的词，与自身词族以及表示可比性的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being equal in value
open to more than one meaning
a person or thing matching another

normalIntro.en: Equivalent is equal plus worth: two unlike things can still balance.
normalIntro.cn: equivalent 是「相等」加「价值」：两个不同的东西也可以彼此平衡。

normal.en: Equivalent to means equal in value or effect.
normal.cn: equivalent to 表示在价值或效果上等于。

normal.en: A silent answer can be equivalent to a yes.
normal.cn: 沉默的回答可能等同于同意。

normal.en: The noun equivalence names the equal state.
normal.cn: 名词 equivalence 指相等的状态。

normal.en: No exact equivalent means there is no perfect match.
normal.cn: no exact equivalent 表示没有完全对应的说法。

normal.en: Compare tantamount: tantamount is mostly about effect, equivalent is broader.
normal.cn: 对比 tantamount：tantamount 多指效果，equivalent 范围更广。

abstract.en: Picture two different coins balancing on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚不同的硬币在天平上保持平衡。

abstract.en: Imagine a translator finding a matching phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象译者找到一个对应的说法。

abstract.en: Think of two roads that lead to the same town.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路通向同一座城镇。

examples.en: Ten dimes are equivalent to one dollar.
examples.cn: 十枚十分硬币等于一美元。

examples.en: For him, losing the match was equivalent to failure.
examples.cn: 对他来说，输掉比赛等同于失败。

examples.en: The Italian word has no equivalent in my language.
examples.cn: 这个意大利语词在我的语言里没有对应词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equi + valent」——两边「价值相等」，就是等值；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（相等的）＋ valere（值）→ aequivalere（价值相等）→ 法语 équivalent → 英语 equivalent，核心义「价值或作用相等」。

sensesIntro.en: Equivalent begins with equal value, extends to equal effect, and then names the matching thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: equivalent 从价值相等开始，扩展到效果相同，再指与之匹配的事物本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two different coins balancing on one scale.
