core.cn: 核心意象：两枚不同的硬币在天平上平衡。

branches.en: Equal value is the literal core sense.
branches.cn: 价值相等是字面核心义项。

branches.en: Equal effect extends worth to results.
branches.cn: 效果相同把价值扩展到结果。

branches.en: The matching thing is the noun use.
branches.cn: 匹配之物是名词用法。

branches.en: Things of equal value often have equal effect.
branches.cn: 价值相等的事物往往效果也相同。

branches.en: A counterpart is the thing that carries equal value.
branches.cn: 对应物就是承载同等价值的事物。

intro.en: Equivalent combines a Latin equal root with a Latin worth root, plus English noun and adverb endings.
intro.cn: equivalent 结合拉丁语「相等」词根与「价值」词根，并加上英语名词和副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus means equal and valere means to be worth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为相等，valere 意为值。

items.exampleCN: equivalent 保留结合后的含义。

definition_en: a long period of history with a particular character
core_image: 一条长河被刻上标记，分成一段段可命名的时期
scene: 铁路的修建开启了这个地区的新时代。The railway opened a new era for the region.
sceneCN: 这里 era 是「时代」（第 1 个义项：具有某种特征的一段长时期）；句意：铁路的修建为这个地区开启了新时代。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a long period of history marked by particular events, ideas, or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 以特定事件、思想或状况为标志的一段长历史时期
senses.example: The invention of printing began a new era.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术的发明开启了一个新时代。
senses.why: The word first meant a system of counting years, so it naturally names a marked stretch of history.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指纪年的体系，因此自然指一段被标记的历史时期。

senses.title: A notable period in a life
senses.definition: a period in a person's life associated with a particular activity or mood
senses.definitionCN: 与某种活动或情绪相关的一段个人生活时期
senses.example: Her teaching era lasted twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教学生涯持续了二十年。
senses.why: A historical era and a personal era are both bounded periods with a character.
senses.whyCN: 历史时代与个人时期都是具有某种特征的有界时期。

senses.title: A geological era
senses.definition: a major division of geological time, longer than a period
senses.definitionCN: 地质时间的主要划分，比「纪」更长
senses.example: Dinosaurs lived in the Mesozoic era.
senses.exampleCN: 恐龙生活在中生代。
senses.why: Geology borrows the general word for a very long, clearly divided span of time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借用这个一般词，指极长且有明确划分的时间跨度。

intro.en: Era comes from Late Latin aera, a system of counting years, probably from Latin aes, bronze or money, whose plural is aera.
intro.cn: era 来自晚期拉丁语 aera（纪年体系），可能源于拉丁语 aes（青铜、钱币），其复数为 aera。

items.en: Aes means bronze or money.
items.cn: aes 意为青铜或钱币。

items.en: Aera is the plural of aes.
items.cn: aera 是 aes 的复数。

items.en: Aera means a system of counting years.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aera 指纪年体系。

items.en: Era carries the dating sense into Romance languages.
items.cn: era 把纪年含义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Modern English broadens era to any notable period.
items.cn: 现代英语把 era 扩展到任何显著时期。

note.en: Era is a period word, with look-alike forms and near words for long spans of time.
note.cn: era 是表示「时期」的词，拥有形近形式以及与长时间跨度相邻的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语 aes 的复数

entries.definition: a period marked by a major change

normalIntro.en: Era is a marked stretch of time: historians draw a line and give the years a name.
normalIntro.cn: era 是一段被标记的时间：历史学家画一条线，再给这些年岁一个名字。

normal.en: A new era begins when something important changes.
normal.cn: 当重要的事物发生变化，新时代就开始了。

normal.en: The digital era is the age of computers and networks.
normal.cn: digital era 是计算机与网络的时代。

normal.en: The plural eras covers several named periods.
normal.cn: 复数 eras 指多个被命名的时期。

normal.en: A geologic era is longer than a period.
normal.cn: 地质年代比「纪」更长。

normal.en: Compare epoch: an epoch is shorter and marked by a sharp change.
normal.cn: 对比 epoch：epoch 更短，以剧烈变化为标志。

abstract.en: Picture a long river with stones marking each stretch.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长河，用石头标出每一段。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar page turning into a bright new color.
abstract.cn: 想象日历翻到崭新明亮的一页。

abstract.en: Think of layers of rock holding the bones of ancient animals.
abstract.cn: 想象岩层中藏着古代动物的骨骼。

examples.en: The internet changed the era of communication.
examples.cn: 互联网改变了通信的时代。

examples.en: Her acting era ended when she moved abroad.
examples.cn: 她移居国外后，演艺时期结束了。

examples.en: The Mesozoic era is famous for its dinosaurs.
examples.cn: 中生代以恐龙闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「era」——像日历上画出的一个「段」，就是时代；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aes（青铜、钱币，复数 aera）→ 晚期拉丁语 aera（纪年体系）→ 英语 era，核心义「被标记的一段长时间」。

sensesIntro.en: Era moves from a dating system to a historical age, then to a personal period, and finally to a geological division.
sensesIntro.cn: era 从纪年体系转为历史时代，再指个人时期，最后指地质年代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long timeline cut into named stretches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长时间线被切成有名称的段落。

branches.en: A historical period is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 历史时期是现代主要义项。

branches.en: A personal period applies the same span to one life.
branches.cn: 个人时期把同样的跨度用于一生。

branches.en: A geological era is the longest technical use.
branches.cn: 地质年代是最长的技术用法。

branches.en: A person can define an era and also have an era of their own.
branches.cn: 一个人可以定义一个时代，也可以拥有自己的时期。

branches.en: Both history and geology divide time into named eras.
branches.cn: 历史学与地质学都把时间划分为有名称的时代。

intro.en: Era is a short Latin-derived noun whose English family grows mainly through compounds.
intro.cn: era 是源自拉丁语的短名词，其英语词族主要通过复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin aes means bronze or money, and its plural aera leads to the dating sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aes 意为青铜或钱币，其复数 aera 引出纪年含义。

items.example: Aes is the older Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: aes 是较早的拉丁语名词。

items.example: Aera becomes the base of era.
items.exampleCN: aera 成为 era 的基础。
era 保留「计数时间」的含义。

items.example: Epoch is a near period word.
Age is the plainer near word.
items.exampleCN: age 是更朴素的近义词。

definition_en: to build something or raise it upright, or standing straight up
core_image: 一根柱子从地面被扶正，笔直地立起来
scene: 工人们在广场上竖起了一座纪念碑。Workers erected a monument in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 erected 是 erect 的过去式，表示「竖立」（第 1 个义项：建造并使其立起）；句意：工人们在广场上竖起了一座纪念碑。

senses.title: To build or set up
senses.definition: to build a structure or set something upright in place
senses.definitionCN: 建造建筑物或把某物立起来安置好
senses.example: They erected a bridge across the narrow river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在狭窄的河上建了一座桥。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to raise up, so building and setting upright share one core action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为向上竖起，因此建造与竖立共享同一个核心动作。

senses.title: To raise into an upright position
senses.definition: to lift or straighten something so that it stands vertically
senses.definitionCN: 把某物抬起或扶正，使其垂直立起
senses.example: The campers erected their tent before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 露营者在天黑前搭好了帐篷。
senses.why: The physical act of raising is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 向上抬起的身体动作，是这个词最古老的含义层。

senses.title: Standing straight up
senses.definition: standing or pointing straight upward, used as an adjective
senses.definitionCN: 笔直站立或指向上方，作形容词使用
senses.example: He sat with an erect back throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中他都挺直着背坐着。
senses.why: The past participle became an adjective describing the upright result.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词转化为形容词，描述竖立后的状态。

intro.en: Erect comes from Latin erigere, to raise up, from e-, out, and regere, to guide or keep straight.
intro.cn: erect 来自拉丁语 erigere（向上竖起），由 e-（向外）与 regere（引导、使直）构成。

items.en: Regere means to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导或使直。

items.en: E- means out or upward here.
items.cn: 这里的 e- 表示向外或向上。

items.en: Erigere means to raise or set upright.
items.cn: erigere 意为竖起、使直立。

items.en: Erectus means upright or straight.
items.cn: erectus 意为竖直的、直的。

items.en: Erect enters English as verb and adjective.
items.cn: erect 作为动词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses erect for building and for posture.
items.cn: 现代英语中，erect 用于建造和姿态。

note.en: Erect is an upright word, close to its noun and adverb family and to verbs for building.
note.cn: erect 是表示「竖直」的词，与自身名词、副词词族以及表示建造的动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of building or raising
a person or device that erects

normalIntro.en: Erect is a raising word: a crane lifts a beam until it stands straight.
normalIntro.cn: erect 是「竖起」词：吊车把横梁吊起，直到它笔直站立。

normal.en: To erect a monument is to set it upright for people to see.
normal.cn: erect a monument 就是把纪念碑竖起来供人瞻仰。

normal.en: Workers erect scaffolding before painting a tall wall.
normal.cn: 工人在粉刷高墙前搭起脚手架。

normal.en: An erect posture means a straight back.
normal.cn: erect posture 指挺直的背。

normal.en: The noun erection can mean the act of building.
normal.cn: 名词 erection 可指建造的动作。

normal.en: Compare build: build is general, erect stresses standing something up.
normal.cn: 对比 build：build 泛指建造，erect 强调把某物立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a stone column rising slowly from the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一根石柱从地面缓缓升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a flagpole pulled straight by ropes.
abstract.cn: 想象旗杆被绳索拉得笔直。

abstract.en: Think of a child standing tall to be measured.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子挺直身子量身高。

examples.en: The city erected a statue in her honor.
examples.cn: 这座城市为她竖立了一座雕像。

examples.en: They erected a fence around the garden.
examples.cn: 他们在花园四周立起了栅栏。

examples.en: He walked with an erect and steady gait.
examples.cn: 他走路时身姿挺直而稳健。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + rect」——把弯的东西「弄直」，就是竖立；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ regere（使直）→ erigere（向上竖起）→ erectus（竖直的）→ 英语 erect，核心义「使直立、竖起」。

sensesIntro.en: Erect begins with building and raising, then describes the act of standing something up, and finally the upright state.
sensesIntro.cn: erect 从建造与竖起开始，再描述把某物立起的动作，最后描述竖直的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column lifted until it stands perfectly straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：柱子被扶起，直到完全笔直。

branches.en: Building and setting up is the main verb sense.
branches.cn: 建造与设立是主要动词义项。

branches.en: Raising upright is the physical action.
branches.cn: 使直立是身体动作。

branches.en: The upright state is the adjective sense.
branches.cn: 竖直状态是形容词义项。

branches.en: To erect a structure is to raise it into place.
branches.cn: 建造结构就是把它们立到位置上。

branches.en: Raising something results in an upright thing.
branches.cn: 把某物竖起，结果就是一件直立之物。

intro.en: Erect is a Latin raising word, with English relatives in erection, erectly, and erector.
intro.cn: erect 是拉丁语中表示「竖起」的词，英语亲属有 erection、erectly 与 erector。

latinIntro.en: Latin erigere means to raise up, from e-, out, and regere, to guide straight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 erigere 意为向上竖起，由 e-（向外）与 regere（使直）构成。

items.meaning: a person or thing that acts

definition_zh: 错误的；不正确的；基于误判的
definition_en: wrong or based on a mistake
core_image: 一个人偏离了直路，走进岔道还以为是正途
scene: 报告里有一个错误的数据，结论因此站不住脚。The report contained an erroneous figure, so its conclusion failed.
sceneCN: 这里 erroneous 是「错误的」（第 1 个义项：事实或内容不正确）；句意：报告里有一个错误的数据，所以结论站不住脚。

pos.zh: 错误的；不正确的；基于误判的

senses.title: Factually wrong
senses.definition: containing a mistake or not matching the facts
senses.definitionCN: 包含错误或与事实不符的
senses.example: The article was based on erroneous data.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章建立在错误的数据之上。
senses.why: The adjective comes from error, whose Latin root means wandering, so a wrong statement has strayed from the truth.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词来自 error，其拉丁词根意为「游荡」，所以错误的陈述偏离了真相。

senses.title: Based on mistaken judgment
senses.definition: formed from a wrong belief, assumption, or way of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误信念、假设或推理方式上的
senses.example: Their conclusion proved erroneous after further study.
senses.exampleCN: 进一步研究后，他们的结论被证明是错的。
senses.why: A mistaken judgment is a path of thought that has wandered off course.
senses.whyCN: 错误的判断就是一条偏离正轨的思路。

intro.en: Erroneous comes from Latin erroneus, wandering, from errare, to wander or stray.
intro.cn: erroneous 来自拉丁语 erroneus（游荡的），源于 errare（漫游、走偏）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or stray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Erroneus means wandering or mistaken.
items.cn: erroneus 意为游荡的、错误的。

items.en: Erroneous enters English with the mistake sense.
items.cn: erroneous 以「错误」的含义进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses erroneous mainly for beliefs and information.
items.cn: 现代英语中，erroneous 主要用于信念和信息。

note.en: Erroneous is the adjective of error, close to its family and to words for being wrong.
note.cn: erroneous 是 error 的形容词，与自身词族以及表示「错误」的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Erroneous comes from wandering: a wrong idea has walked off the true path.
normalIntro.cn: erroneous 来自「游荡」：错误的想法走离了正确的道路。

normal.en: Erroneous data leads to bad decisions.
normal.cn: 错误的数据导致糟糕的决定。

normal.en: An erroneous belief is a belief that is not true.
normal.cn: erroneous belief 是不符合事实的信念。

normal.en: The adverb erroneously means by mistake.
normal.cn: 副词 erroneously 表示错误地。

normal.en: The noun error is the simpler relative.
normal.cn: 名词 error 是更简单的亲属词。

normal.en: Compare mistaken: mistaken stresses the person, erroneous stresses the content.
normal.cn: 对比 mistaken：mistaken 强调人，erroneous 强调内容。

abstract.en: Picture a traveler taking the wrong fork in a road.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人在岔路口走错了方向。

abstract.en: Imagine a map with one line drawn in the wrong place.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上有一条线画错了位置。

abstract.en: Think of a calculator showing a number that cannot be right.
abstract.cn: 想象计算器显示出一个不可能正确的数字。

examples.en: The rumor turned out to be erroneous.
examples.cn: 那个谣言最终被证明是错的。

examples.en: An erroneous assumption ruined the whole plan.
examples.cn: 一个错误的假设毁掉了整个计划。

examples.en: Please correct any erroneous entries in the list.
examples.cn: 请更正清单中任何错误的条目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「error + neous」——带着「错误」的形容词，就是错误的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（错误）→ erroneus（游荡的、错误的）→ 英语 erroneous，核心义「偏离正途而错」。

sensesIntro.en: Erroneous first describes wrong facts or statements, and then wrong beliefs or ways of reasoning.
sensesIntro.cn: erroneous 先描述错误的事实或陈述，再描述错误的信念或推理方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path that has strayed away from the true road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条偏离正路的岔道。

branches.en: Wrong content is the main factual sense.
branches.cn: 内容错误是主要事实义项。

branches.en: Wrong judgment applies straying to reasoning.
branches.cn: 误判把「走偏」用于推理。

branches.en: Bad data and bad assumptions both lead reasoning astray.
branches.cn: 坏数据与坏假设都会把推理带偏。

branches.en: A statement and a figure can both be erroneous.
branches.cn: 陈述与数字都可能是错误的。

branches.en: A belief and a conclusion can both rest on error.
branches.cn: 信念与结论都可能建立在错误之上。

intro.en: Erroneous is a Latin wandering adjective, with English relatives error, erroneously, and erroneousness.
intro.cn: erroneous 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的形容词，英语亲属有 error、erroneously 与 erroneousness。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

definition_en: a mistake, or the state of being wrong
core_image: 一支箭偏出靶心，落在旁边的空处
scene: 表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。A small error in the table made the total wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 error 是「错误」（第 1 个义项：做错或写错的地方）；句意：表格里有一个小错误，导致总数不对。

senses.title: A mistake
senses.definition: something done or written wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 做错或写错的事情
senses.example: She spotted an error in the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现第一行有一个错误。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a wandering, so an error is a step that has strayed from the right way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词意为「游荡」，所以错误就是偏离正路的一步。

senses.title: The state of being wrong
senses.definition: the condition of holding a wrong belief or being mistaken
senses.definitionCN: 持有错误看法或弄错的状态
senses.example: I was in error about the meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 我把会议时间弄错了。
senses.why: The word can name not only the mistake but the condition of being mistaken.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅指错误本身，也可以指弄错的状态。

senses.title: A measured deviation
senses.definition: a difference between a measured or calculated value and the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算值与真实值之间的差异
senses.example: The experiment allows a small margin of error.
senses.exampleCN: 这项实验允许有一个小的误差范围。
senses.why: Scientific use turns the general mistake into a measurable deviation.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法把一般性的错误转化为可测量的偏差。

intro.en: Error comes from Latin error, a wandering or mistake, from errare, to wander.
intro.cn: error 来自拉丁语 error（游荡、错误），源于 errare（漫游）。

items.en: Errare means to wander or go astray.
items.cn: errare 意为游荡、走偏。

items.en: Error means a wandering or a mistake.
items.cn: error 意为游荡或错误。

items.en: Errur carries the word into French.
items.cn: errur 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Error names a mistake in English.
items.cn: 中古英语 error 指错误。

items.en: Modern English adds scientific and computing errors.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了科学误差与计算机错误。

note.en: Error is the noun of straying, close to err, erroneous, and to ordinary mistake words.
note.cn: error 是表示「走偏」的名词，与 err、erroneous 以及普通的「错误」词相邻。

entries.definition: a defect or responsibility for wrong

normalIntro.en: Error is a wandering step: the mind or hand leaves the straight road for a moment.
normalIntro.cn: error 是走偏的一步：头脑或手在一瞬间离开了直路。

normal.en: To make an error is to get something wrong.
normal.cn: make an error 就是把某事弄错。

normal.en: Human error causes many accidents.
normal.cn: 人为失误造成许多事故。

normal.en: An error message tells you the program failed.
normal.cn: error message 告诉你程序出错了。

normal.en: In error means by mistake.
normal.cn: in error 表示错误地。

normal.en: Compare mistake: mistake is everyday, error is slightly more formal and technical.
normal.cn: 对比 mistake：mistake 更日常，error 稍正式且更技术化。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow landing just beside the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭落在靶心旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine a pen slipping on a single letter.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖在一个字母上滑了一下。

abstract.en: Think of a clock running a few seconds fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟快了几秒钟。

examples.en: The report contains several spelling errors.
examples.cn: 报告里有几处拼写错误。

examples.en: He sent the parcel to the wrong address in error.
examples.cn: 他误把包裹寄到了错误的地址。

examples.en: Scientists try to reduce the margin of error.
examples.cn: 科学家努力缩小误差范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「err + or」——走「偏」了，就是犯错；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 errare（游荡、走偏）→ error（游荡；错误）→ 古法语 errur → 英语 error，核心义「偏离正途」。

sensesIntro.en: Error first means a wrong act or word, then the state of being mistaken, and finally a measurable deviation.
sensesIntro.cn: error 先指做错的事或写错的地方，再指弄错的状态，最后指可测量的误差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow that lands beside the target.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭落在靶心旁边。

branches.en: A concrete mistake is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 具体的错误是日常义项。

branches.en: Being mistaken is the state sense.
branches.cn: 弄错的状态是状态义项。

branches.en: A measured deviation is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 测量偏差是技术义项。

branches.en: A person in error often makes a visible mistake.
branches.cn: 处于错误中的人往往会犯下可见的错误。

branches.en: Both a slip and a margin of error are deviations from the true value.
branches.cn: 小失误与误差范围都是对真实值的偏离。

intro.en: Error is a Latin wandering noun, with English err, erroneous, and errorless built around it.
intro.cn: error 是拉丁语中表示「走偏」的名词，英语围绕它构成 err、erroneous 与 errorless。

latinIntro.en: Latin errare means to wander, and error means a wandering or mistake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 errare 意为游荡，error 意为游荡或错误。

items.example: Err is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: err 是简短的英语动词。
